# 7.5 Fully maximal random-effects model (registered)

```{r lmm-fully-maximal}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fully maximal random-effects structure (registered):
#
#   rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 + stimulus_type | id)
#                                 + (1 + Type | stimulus_id)
#
# Why it is fitted. The usual objection to a 10-stimulus design that claims
# a general "AI penalty" is stimulus sampling: the effect might belong to
# these particular images. The intercepts-only primary model tests Type
# against participant sampling variance only (denominator degrees of
# freedom DenDF = 109 = N - 2), and so treats the 10 images as a fixed set.
# The by-stimulus random slope for Type lets each image have its own
# AI-vs-Human gap. The SD of those gaps is the quantity the objection asks
# for, and the fixed effect in this model is tested against both participant
# and stimulus sampling variance (Judd, Westfall & Kenny, 2012; Barr et al.,
# 2013). See the comments in §7 and §7.4 for why this term is estimable.
#
# Expected outcome: the fit is singular for both dimensions. Singular here
# means that at least one correlation in the structure sits at plus or minus
# one: the by-image intercept and Type slope correlate at -1 on both
# dimensions, and on effort the by-participant intercept and stimulus_type
# slope correlate at +1. It does not mean the slopes are zero. The by-stimulus
# Type-slope SD is small but estimated (~0.08 creativity, ~0.02 effort,
# against attribution effects of about 0.45 and 0.92 rating points), and the
# by-participant stimulus_type slope SD is ~0.15 (creativity) and ~0.04
# (effort). The fixed effects equal the primary model's to the third decimal,
# and so does the registered H1 contrast (human minus generator, averaged
# over image kind: 0.448 creativity, 0.921 effort), with a standard error
# that rises only slightly for creativity (0.131 against 0.128). What this
# answers is narrower than "the penalty does not vary across images": with
# ten images the spread of the penalty from image to image is estimated as
# small, the estimate of that spread is not well pinned down, and allowing for
# it leaves the attribution effect and its standard error close to the
# primary model's. The intercepts-only model is therefore reported as primary
# (it is not singular and its numbers are the verified headline results), and
# this section is cited for the stimulus-generalization question. Report
# singularity as estimated rather than tuning it away with an optimizer.
#
# Optimizer: bobyqa first, as in the primary model. Fall back to Nelder-Mead
# only on an error or a non-convergence warning, not on singularity, which is
# a property of the data and not of the optimizer.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_lmm_fully_maximal.csv"),
              file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS,
                        c("study1_lmm_creativity_fullymaximal.rds",
                          "study1_lmm_effort_fullymaximal.rds")))

FORMULA_FULLY_MAXIMAL <- rating ~ Type * stimulus_type +
  (1 + stimulus_type | id) + (1 + Type | stimulus_id)

fit_fully_maximal_lmm <- function(dim_name, data = long) {

  dat_sub <- data %>% filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating))
  dat_sub$Type          <- relevel(factor(dat_sub$Type),          ref = "Human")
  dat_sub$stimulus_type <- relevel(factor(dat_sub$stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure")

  try_fit <- function(optimizer) {
    warns <- character(0)
    fit <- withCallingHandlers(
      tryCatch(
        lmerTest::lmer(FORMULA_FULLY_MAXIMAL, data = dat_sub, REML = TRUE,
                       control = lmerControl(optimizer = optimizer,
                                             optCtrl   = list(maxfun = 2e5))),
        error = function(e) e),
      warning = function(w) {
        warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      })
    list(fit = fit, warnings = warns, optimizer = optimizer)
  }

  res <- try_fit("bobyqa")
  failed <- inherits(res$fit, "error") ||
    any(grepl("failed to converge|convergence", res$warnings, ignore.case = TRUE))
  if (failed) {
    res_nm <- try_fit("Nelder_Mead")
    res_nm$bobyqa_warnings <- res$warnings
    res <- res_nm
  }

  # The status reads the warnings captured above as well as lme4's own
  # messages, so a convergence warning raised by the fit is not lost.
  res$status <- lmer_fit_status(res$fit, res$warnings)

  if (inherits(res$fit, "error")) {
    res$singular <- NA
    res$by_stim_type_slope_sd <- NA_real_
    return(res)
  }

  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(res$fit))
  slope_row <- vc %>% filter(grp == "stimulus_id", var1 == "TypeAI", is.na(var2))
  res$singular              <- lme4::isSingular(res$fit, tol = 1e-4)
  res$varcorr               <- vc
  res$by_stim_type_slope_sd <- if (nrow(slope_row) == 1) slope_row$sdcor else NA_real_
  res
}

fullmax_creat <- fit_fully_maximal_lmm("creativity")
fullmax_eff   <- fit_fully_maximal_lmm("effort")

report_fullmax <- function(res, primary_res, dim_name) {
  cat("\n=== Fully maximal LMM:", dim_name, "===\n")
  cat("Optimizer used:", res$optimizer, "\n")
  if (length(res$warnings)) cat("lme4 messages:", paste(res$warnings, collapse = " | "), "\n")
  if (inherits(res$fit, "error")) {
    cat("Fit FAILED:", conditionMessage(res$fit), "\n"); return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("Singular fit:", res$singular, "\n")
  cat("By-stimulus Type-slope SD:", signif(res$by_stim_type_slope_sd, 3), "\n")
  cat("\nVariance components:\n"); print(res$varcorr)
  cat("\nFixed effects (fully maximal):\n"); print(summary(res$fit)$coefficients)
  cat("\nvs. primary (intercepts-only) model:\n")
  print(primary_res$coef_table %>% select(term, estimate, std.error, p.value))
}
report_fullmax(fullmax_creat, creativity_res, "creativity")
report_fullmax(fullmax_eff,   effort_res,     "effort")

# Side-by-side table for the supplement. The columns other files rely on are
# dimension, term, est_primary, est_maximal, se_maximal, p_maximal,
# by_stim_type_slope_sd,
# singular, optimizer, followed by the maximal fit's status (converged,
# fit_error, lme4_messages, fit_note). The last row of each dimension is the
# registered H1 contrast, human minus generator averaged over image kind, with
# Satterthwaite degrees of freedom to match the coefficient rows; it is the
# row that answers the stimulus-sampling question for the headline quantity.
# If the maximal fit errored or did not converge, p_maximal is set to NA and
# fit_note says why.
fullmax_table_for <- function(res, primary_res, dim_name) {
  prim <- primary_res$coef_table %>% select(term, est_primary = estimate) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(term = H1_CONTRAST_LABEL,
                     est_primary = h1_contrast(primary_res$fit,
                                               "satterthwaite")$estimate))
  status_cols <- function(tbl) {
    tbl %>% mutate(converged     = res$status$converged,
                   fit_error     = res$status$fit_error,
                   lme4_messages = res$status$lme4_messages,
                   fit_note      = fit_note(res$status,
                                            "maximal-structure p-value"))
  }
  if (inherits(res$fit, "error")) {
    return(prim %>% mutate(dimension = dim_name, est_maximal = NA_real_,
                           se_maximal = NA_real_, p_maximal = NA_real_,
                           by_stim_type_slope_sd = NA_real_, singular = NA,
                           optimizer = paste0(res$optimizer, " (FAILED)")) %>%
             status_cols() %>%
             relocate(dimension))
  }
  h1_m <- h1_contrast(res$fit, "satterthwaite")
  maxi <- broom.mixed::tidy(res$fit, effects = "fixed") %>%
    select(term, est_maximal = estimate, se_maximal = std.error, p_maximal = p.value) %>%
    bind_rows(tibble(term = H1_CONTRAST_LABEL, est_maximal = h1_m$estimate,
                     se_maximal = h1_m$se, p_maximal = h1_m$p))
  out <- prim %>%
    left_join(maxi, by = "term") %>%
    mutate(dimension             = dim_name,
           by_stim_type_slope_sd = res$by_stim_type_slope_sd,
           singular              = res$singular,
           optimizer             = res$optimizer) %>%
    status_cols() %>%
    relocate(dimension, term, est_primary, est_maximal, se_maximal, p_maximal,
             by_stim_type_slope_sd, singular, optimizer)
  if (!fit_usable(res$status)) out$p_maximal <- NA_real_
  out
}
fully_maximal_table <- bind_rows(
  fullmax_table_for(fullmax_creat, creativity_res, "creativity"),
  fullmax_table_for(fullmax_eff,   effort_res,     "effort")
)
fully_maximal_table
write_csv(fully_maximal_table,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_lmm_fully_maximal.csv"))

# The H1 contrast row should show est_primary == est_maximal to 3 decimal
# places on both dimensions. If they diverge by more than ~0.01, the stimulus
# slope is absorbing something and the manuscript sentence must change.
if (!inherits(fullmax_creat$fit, "error")) {
  saveRDS(fullmax_creat,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_creativity_fullymaximal.rds"))
}
if (!inherits(fullmax_eff$fit, "error")) {
  saveRDS(fullmax_eff,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_effort_fullymaximal.rds"))
}
```

# 7.6 Joint model: the formal test of the comparative claim (H2) (registered)

```{r lmm-joint}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Joint two-dimension model (registered).
#
# Why a joint model. The manuscript's central comparative claim is that the
# AI penalty is larger for effort than for creativity (sweat of the brow is
# hit harder than Feist's minimal spark). Sections 7.1/7.2 fit creativity and
# effort in separate models, and separate models cannot test that claim: two
# significant effects of different size are not evidence that the sizes
# differ. Every participant rated every stimulus on both dimensions, and the
# two are strongly related (r ~ .79 between participants' creativity and
# effort means). The test therefore stacks both dimensions in one model, with
# `dimension` as a within-participant factor, and reads the Type x dimension
# interaction.
#
# Model (registered):
#   rating ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type
#            + (1 + dimension | id)             by-participant intercept and
#                                               creativity-vs-effort slope
#            + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)      one intercept per image per
#                                               dimension (an image can be
#                                               "effortful-looking" without
#                                               being "creative-looking")
# If that structure is singular, the registered fallback is
#   (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)
# and the output says which one was used.
#
# H2 test: the Type:dimension term of the type-III Satterthwaite ANOVA.
# H1, that attribution lowers ratings on each dimension taken on its own, is
# tested in sections 7.1 and 7.2 by the estimated marginal attribution
# contrast within each per-dimension model. This section asks whether the two
# effects differ in size, which is a separate question and a separate
# prediction.
# Expected: F(1, 109) ~ 23.0, p ~ 5e-6.
#
# Whether the two scales can be compared. Both DVs (dependent variables, the
# measured outcomes) are 1-5 ratings collected on the same instrument, on the
# same trial, for the same image, and on nineteen of the
# twenty items the anchors run in parallel ("No ... involved", "Minimal",
# "Moderate", "Significant", "A great deal of ... involved"). The exception
# is the effort item for the first figurative image, 1FigureEff, whose 4 and
# 5 read "A lot of effort involved" and "Significant effort involved" (see
# section 1.3). Apart from that item, a one-point difference is anchored the
# same way on both dimensions, and that is what licenses comparing the two
# Type effects in rating units; section 7.11 refits this contrast without
# the item. It does not license claiming that creativity and effort are
# psychologically equally "wide" constructs; the per-dimension models
# (§7.1/7.2) remain the interpretable decomposition and are what the results
# section describes first.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB,
                        c("study1_joint_model_anova.csv",
                          "study1_joint_model_fixed.csv",
                          "study1_joint_model_contrast_of_contrasts.csv",
                          "study1_joint_model_simple_effects.csv")),
              file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_joint.rds"))

joint_dat <- long %>%
  filter(!is.na(rating)) %>%
  mutate(
    Type          = relevel(factor(Type),          ref = "Human"),
    dimension     = factor(dimension, levels = DIM_LEVELS),   # creativity = ref
    stimulus_type = relevel(factor(stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure"),
    stim_dim      = interaction(stimulus_id, dimension, drop = TRUE)
  )
stopifnot(nlevels(joint_dat$stim_dim) == 20,
          n_distinct(joint_dat$id) == nrow(dat))

JOINT_CTRL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

joint_fit_full <- tryCatch(
  lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type +
                   (1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stim_dim),
                 data = joint_dat, REML = TRUE, control = JOINT_CTRL),
  error = function(e) e)

joint_structure <- "(1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)"
if (inherits(joint_fit_full, "error") ||
    lme4::isSingular(joint_fit_full, tol = 1e-4)) {
  cat("Joint model with by-participant dimension slope is",
      if (inherits(joint_fit_full, "error")) "unfittable" else "SINGULAR",
      "and the registered intercepts-only structure is fitted instead.\n")
  joint_fit <- lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type +
                                (1 | id) + (1 | stim_dim),
                              data = joint_dat, REML = TRUE, control = JOINT_CTRL)
  joint_structure <- "(1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)  [fallback: full structure singular]"
} else {
  joint_fit <- joint_fit_full
}
cat("Joint model random-effects structure used:", joint_structure, "\n")
cat("Singular:", lme4::isSingular(joint_fit, tol = 1e-4), "\n")
# The fit's convergence status (lmer_fit_status(), section 7). Every table
# this chunk writes carries it, and its p-values are set to NA if the fit did
# not converge.
joint_status <- lmer_fit_status(joint_fit)
cat("Converged:", joint_status$converged,
    "| lme4 messages:", if (nzchar(joint_status$lme4_messages))
                          joint_status$lme4_messages else "none", "\n")

joint_anova <- anova(joint_fit, type = "III", ddf = "Satterthwaite")
cat("\n=== Joint model: type-III ANOVA (Satterthwaite) ===\n")
print(joint_anova)
cat("\nH2 test (Type x dimension):\n")
print(joint_anova["Type:dimension", , drop = FALSE])

joint_anova_tbl <- as.data.frame(joint_anova) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  mutate(random_structure = joint_structure,
         singular = lme4::isSingular(joint_fit, tol = 1e-4)) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  with_status(joint_status, "Pr(>F)")
joint_fixed_tbl <- broom.mixed::tidy(joint_fit, effects = "fixed", conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(random_structure = joint_structure) %>%
  with_status(joint_status, "p.value")

# Simple effects of Type within each dimension (averaged over stimulus_type)
# and the contrast of contrasts, the difference between those two simple
# effects: (Human - AI | effort) - (Human - AI | creativity). Positive = the
# AI penalty is larger for effort. Satterthwaite df to match the ANOVA;
# Kenward-Roger would be the emmeans default and is slower on 2,220 rows
# with no practical difference here.
joint_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(joint_fit, ~ Type | dimension,
                              lmer.df = "satterthwaite")
joint_pairs <- pairs(joint_emm, adjust = "none")   # 2-level factor: nothing to adjust
cat("\n=== Joint model: Type simple effects by dimension ===\n")
print(joint_pairs)

joint_emm_2way <- emmeans::emmeans(joint_fit, ~ Type * dimension,
                                   lmer.df = "satterthwaite")
joint_coc <- emmeans::contrast(joint_emm_2way,
                               interaction = c(Type = "pairwise",
                                               dimension = "revpairwise"))
cat("\n=== Joint model: contrast of contrasts (effort Type-effect minus creativity Type-effect) ===\n")
print(joint_coc)
print(confint(joint_coc))

# summary() carries the test (SE, df, t, p); confint() carries the CI. Both
# return their rows in the same order, so their columns are bound side by
# side rather than joined.
joint_coc_tbl <- bind_cols(
  as.data.frame(summary(joint_coc)),
  as.data.frame(confint(joint_coc)) %>% select(lower.CL, upper.CL)
) %>%
  mutate(definition = "(Human - AI | effort) - (Human - AI | creativity); positive = larger AI penalty for effort",
         random_structure = joint_structure) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  with_status(joint_status, "p.value")
joint_pairs_tbl <- bind_cols(
  as.data.frame(summary(joint_pairs)),
  as.data.frame(confint(joint_pairs)) %>% select(lower.CL, upper.CL)
) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  with_status(joint_status, "p.value")
stopifnot(nrow(joint_coc_tbl) == 1, !anyNA(joint_coc_tbl$estimate),
          nrow(joint_pairs_tbl) == 2)

write_csv(joint_anova_tbl, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_joint_model_anova.csv"))
write_csv(joint_fixed_tbl, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_joint_model_fixed.csv"))
write_csv(joint_coc_tbl,   file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_joint_model_contrast_of_contrasts.csv"))
write_csv(joint_pairs_tbl, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_joint_model_simple_effects.csv"))

saveRDS(list(fit = joint_fit, structure = joint_structure, anova = joint_anova,
             emm = joint_emm, pairs = joint_pairs, contrast_of_contrasts = joint_coc,
             fit_full_attempt = joint_fit_full, status = joint_status),
        file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_lmm_joint.rds"))
# Interpretation note: the Type simple effects here are emmeans contrasts
# averaged over stimulus_type, so as Human - AI they equal
# -(TypeAI + 0.5 * TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure) from the per-dimension models,
# not the reference-level TypeAI coefficient. Expected: Human - AI = 0.448
# (creativity; per-dimension -0.408 + 0.5 * -0.081) and 0.921 (effort;
# -0.911 + 0.5 * -0.020); contrast of contrasts +0.47 [0.28, 0.67],
# t(109) = 4.80, p = 5.1e-6; Type:dimension F(1, 109) = 23.02. The full
# structure (1 + dimension | id) is not singular, so no fallback is needed.
```

## 7.6.1 The same contrast as ordered categories

The joint model above treats a rating of 4 as exactly one point above a 3
and one point below a 5. That is an assumption, and it bears on H2 in a
particular way: under human attribution the two dimensions start at
different levels, so the one further from the scale's floor has more room
to fall, and part of a larger raw drop on effort could be that. The
registered answer is to run the same attribution-by-dimension contrast a
second time in a model that treats the five responses as ordered categories
with no fixed spacing between them, and to claim H2 only if the two versions
agree in sign and in significance.

```{r lmm-joint-ordinal}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The second registered version of the H2 test.
#
# A cumulative-link mixed model treats the five response options as ordered
# categories rather than as equally spaced numbers. It supposes one continuous
# scale underneath the ratings, the latent scale, cut by four thresholds
# into the five categories a participant can tick, and it estimates how far
# each predictor moves a participant along that underlying scale. The
# thresholds are estimated from the data, so if the response options are
# unevenly spaced, or the low end of the scale is compressed, that is absorbed
# by the thresholds rather than by the effect. "Mixed" means it carries the
# same random effects as the joint model of section 7.6: a by-participant
# intercept and creativity-versus-effort slope, and one intercept per image
# per dimension. The link is the logit, so effects on the latent scale are in
# log-odds units: a shift of one unit multiplies by e, about 2.7, the odds of
# a rating falling above any given category rather than at or below it.
#
# Why this matters for H2. H2 says the attribution penalty is larger on effort
# than on creativity. Under human attribution the two dimensions start at
# different levels, so the one further from the floor has more room to fall on
# the raw scale, and a larger raw drop on effort could partly be that. On the
# latent scale the floor is handled by the thresholds, so a larger effort
# penalty there cannot be an artefact of range. The registration therefore
# asks for the contrast in both versions and claims H2 only if they agree in
# sign and in significance; a disagreement is reported as a failure of H2 with
# the range explanation named.
#
# The contrast. Both rows of the table are the same quantity: (human minus
# generator on effort) minus (human minus generator on creativity), averaged
# over image kind, positive when the penalty is larger for effort. The
# raw-scale row is read from `joint_coc_tbl`, the contrast of contrasts that
# section 7.6 computed on the joint model fitted there, in rating points with
# Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; nothing is refitted. The ordinal row is the
# same emmeans interaction contrast on the cumulative-link fit, on the latent
# scale, with a normal reference distribution (a z rather than a t). That is
# what a Laplace-approximated ordinal fit supports. The Laplace approximation
# replaces the exact but intractable integral over the random effects with a
# normal approximation around its peak, so it supplies standard errors but no
# degrees of freedom to attach to a t.
#
# Random structure and fallback. The registered structure is
#   (1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)
# A fit counts as not converged when the optimiser returns a non-zero code,
# when it raises a warning about convergence or about the Hessian (the matrix
# of second derivatives of the log-likelihood at the solution, from which the
# standard errors are read), or when it stops with an error. If that fit does
# not converge, the registered fallback is
#   (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)
# and the table records which structure was used. The table also carries the
# largest absolute gradient at the solution, the steepest slope of the
# log-likelihood left where the optimiser stopped, which is zero at a true
# maximum. It shows how close the optimiser came to a stationary point, a
# point where every such slope is zero.
#
# Convergence gates the verdict. Each row carries its fit's convergence,
# singularity and error status. A row whose fit errored or did not converge
# has its p-value and its significance flag set to NA, with a note, and the
# agreement flag is then NA on both rows, so a contrast from an invalid fit
# can never count toward H2.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h2_ordinal.csv"),
              file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_clmm_joint.rds"))

# A cumulative-link fit is called singular on a definition close to lme4's:
# a random-effect standard deviation below 1e-4 on the latent scale, or a
# random-effect correlation within 1e-4 of plus or minus one.
clmm_singular <- function(fit) {
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) return(NA)
  vc <- ordinal::VarCorr(fit)
  any(vapply(vc, function(m) {
    sds  <- attr(m, "stddev")
    cors <- attr(m, "correlation")
    any(sds < 1e-4) ||
      (!is.null(cors) && any(abs(cors[upper.tri(cors)]) > 1 - 1e-4))
  }, logical(1)))
}

ordinal_dat <- joint_dat %>%
  mutate(rating_ord = factor(rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE))

fit_joint_clmm <- function(formula) {
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(ordinal::clmm(formula, data = ordinal_dat, link = "logit",
                           Hess = TRUE),
             error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed    <- inherits(fit, "error")
  converged <- !failed &&
    isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
    !any(grepl("converge|Hessian|singular", warns, ignore.case = TRUE))
  list(fit = fit, warnings = warns, converged = converged,
       max_abs_gradient  = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)),
       optimizer_message = if (failed) conditionMessage(fit)
                           else fit$optRes$message)
}

ORDINAL_STRUCTURE_FULL     <- "(1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)"
ORDINAL_STRUCTURE_FALLBACK <- "(1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)"

joint_clmm <- fit_joint_clmm(rating_ord ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type +
                               (1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stim_dim))
ordinal_structure <- ORDINAL_STRUCTURE_FULL
ordinal_fell_back <- FALSE
if (!joint_clmm$converged) {
  cat("Ordinal joint model with the by-participant dimension slope did not",
      "converge (", joint_clmm$optimizer_message, "), so it is refitted with the",
      "registered fallback structure.\n")
  joint_clmm <- fit_joint_clmm(rating_ord ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type +
                                 (1 | id) + (1 | stim_dim))
  ordinal_structure <- paste0(ORDINAL_STRUCTURE_FALLBACK,
                              "  [fallback: full structure did not converge]")
  ordinal_fell_back <- TRUE
}
cat("Ordinal joint model random-effects structure used:", ordinal_structure, "\n")
cat("Converged:", joint_clmm$converged,
    "| optimiser message:", joint_clmm$optimizer_message,
    "| largest absolute gradient:", signif(joint_clmm$max_abs_gradient, 3), "\n")
if (length(joint_clmm$warnings)) {
  cat("Warnings raised by the fit:",
      paste(joint_clmm$warnings, collapse = " | "), "\n")
}
if (!inherits(joint_clmm$fit, "error")) {
  cat("\n=== Ordinal joint model: fixed effects on the latent scale ===\n")
  print(coef(summary(joint_clmm$fit)))
  cat("\nVariance components:\n")
  print(ordinal::VarCorr(joint_clmm$fit))
}

# The two rows. The raw-scale row is the section 7.6 object; the ordinal row
# is the same contrast on the cumulative-link fit.
h2_raw_row <- tibble(
  version        = "raw_scale",
  scale          = "rating points (linear mixed model, section 7.6)",
  estimate       = joint_coc_tbl$estimate[1],
  SE             = joint_coc_tbl$SE[1],
  df             = joint_coc_tbl$df[1],
  statistic      = joint_coc_tbl$t.ratio[1],
  statistic_type = "t (Satterthwaite df)",
  p              = joint_coc_tbl$p.value[1],
  random_structure_used = joint_structure,
  converged      = joint_status$converged,
  max_abs_gradient = NA_real_,
  singular       = joint_status$singular,
  fit_error      = joint_status$fit_error,
  fit_messages   = joint_status$lme4_messages,
  note           = fit_note(joint_status)
)

h2_ordinal_row <- tryCatch({
  if (inherits(joint_clmm$fit, "error")) {
    stop("ordinal fit failed: ", conditionMessage(joint_clmm$fit))
  }
  em_ord  <- emmeans::emmeans(joint_clmm$fit, ~ Type * dimension,
                              mode = "latent")
  coc_ord <- emmeans::contrast(em_ord,
                               interaction = c(Type      = "pairwise",
                                               dimension = "revpairwise"))
  s <- as.data.frame(summary(coc_ord))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1)
  cat("\n=== Ordinal joint model: contrast of contrasts on the latent scale ===\n")
  print(coc_ord)
  print(confint(coc_ord))
  tibble(version        = "ordinal",
         scale          = "log-odds on the latent scale (cumulative-link mixed model)",
         estimate       = s$estimate,
         SE             = s$SE,
         df             = s$df,
         statistic      = s$z.ratio,
         statistic_type = "z",
         p              = if (joint_clmm$converged) s$p.value else NA_real_,
         random_structure_used = ordinal_structure,
         converged      = joint_clmm$converged,
         max_abs_gradient = joint_clmm$max_abs_gradient,
         singular       = clmm_singular(joint_clmm$fit),
         fit_error      = FALSE,
         fit_messages   = paste(c(joint_clmm$optimizer_message,
                                  joint_clmm$warnings), collapse = " | "),
         note           = if (joint_clmm$converged) ""
                          else "fit did not converge, so the p-value is set to NA")
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Ordinal H2 contrast unavailable: ", conditionMessage(e))
  tibble(version        = "ordinal",
         scale          = "log-odds on the latent scale (cumulative-link mixed model)",
         estimate       = NA_real_, SE = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
         statistic      = NA_real_, statistic_type = "z", p = NA_real_,
         random_structure_used = ordinal_structure,
         converged      = FALSE,
         max_abs_gradient = NA_real_,
         singular       = NA,
         fit_error      = TRUE,
         fit_messages   = conditionMessage(e),
         note           = "ordinal contrast unavailable, so the p-value is NA")
})

h2_ordinal <- bind_rows(h2_raw_row, h2_ordinal_row) %>%
  mutate(sign = case_when(is.na(estimate) ~ NA_character_,
                          estimate > 0    ~ "positive",
                          estimate < 0    ~ "negative",
                          TRUE            ~ "zero"),
         significant_at_05 = p < .05,
         definition = paste0("(Human - AI | effort) - (Human - AI | creativity), ",
                             "averaged over image kind; positive = larger AI ",
                             "penalty for effort")) %>%
  # One flag, repeated on both rows: the same sign on both and the same
  # significance decision on both. It is NA, not FALSE, when either row's fit
  # errored or did not converge, because no agreement can then be read.
  mutate(agree_sign_and_significance =
           if (!all(converged %in% TRUE) || any(fit_error %in% TRUE) ||
               anyNA(sign) || anyNA(significant_at_05)) NA
           else n_distinct(sign) == 1 && n_distinct(significant_at_05) == 1) %>%
  relocate(version, scale, estimate, SE, df, statistic, statistic_type, p,
           sign, significant_at_05, random_structure_used, converged,
           max_abs_gradient, agree_sign_and_significance, definition)

cat("\n=== H2 in its two registered versions ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h2_ordinal %>%
  select(version, estimate, SE, statistic, statistic_type, p, sign,
         significant_at_05, converged, agree_sign_and_significance) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

# The verdict in words. The agreement condition of H2 is met only if both
# versions come from converged fits, agree, and point the predicted way: a
# positive contrast, significant at .05. That condition is necessary but not
# the whole claim: the raw-scale test is also one of the four tests of the
# confirmatory family and has to survive the Holm correction section 7.9
# applies, so the sentence printed here says so rather than claiming H2 on
# an uncorrected p-value.
h2_agree_raw      <- h2_ordinal$agree_sign_and_significance[1]
h2_agree          <- isTRUE(h2_agree_raw)
h2_both_predicted <- h2_agree &&
  all(h2_ordinal$sign == "positive") && all(h2_ordinal$significant_at_05)
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "\nH2 verdict: the raw-scale contrast is %s and %s (p = %.3g); the ordinal ",
  "contrast is %s and %s (p = %.3g). %s%s\n"),
  h2_ordinal$sign[1],
  ifelse(isTRUE(h2_ordinal$significant_at_05[1]), "significant", "not significant"),
  h2_ordinal$p[1],
  h2_ordinal$sign[2],
  ifelse(isTRUE(h2_ordinal$significant_at_05[2]), "significant", "not significant"),
  h2_ordinal$p[2],
  if (is.na(h2_agree_raw)) {
    "At least one version rests on a fit that errored or did not converge, so no agreement can be read and H2 is not claimed from this table."
  } else if (h2_both_predicted) {
    "The two versions agree in sign and in significance, in the predicted direction, so the agreement condition of H2 is met; the claim also needs the raw-scale test to survive the Holm correction in section 7.9."
  } else if (h2_agree) {
    "The two versions agree with each other but not with the prediction, so H2 is not claimed."
  } else {
    "The two versions disagree, so H2 is not claimed; the disagreement is reported as a failure of H2 with the range explanation named."
  },
  if (ordinal_fell_back) {
    " The ordinal version rests on the fallback random structure, participant intercept only, because the by-participant dimension slope did not converge."
  } else ""))

write_csv(h2_ordinal, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h2_ordinal.csv"))
if (!inherits(joint_clmm$fit, "error")) {
  saveRDS(list(fit = joint_clmm$fit, structure = ordinal_structure,
               converged = joint_clmm$converged,
               warnings = joint_clmm$warnings),
          file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, "study1_clmm_joint.rds"))
}
```

# 7.7 Assumption and influence diagnostics (registered)

```{r lmm-diagnostics, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostics for the two primary fits (registered). The LMM assumes one
# residual variance for both arms (homoscedasticity: equal spread of the
# residuals across conditions). On these data that assumption is violated
# for the participant means (AI:Human variance ratio 3.27, p = 2e-5 for
# effort; see (b) below for the direction), while residual normality is
# fine (skew -0.14 / -0.40). This section puts the checks in the output so
# a reader can see them. It (a) draws the standard plots, (b) tabulates
# residual SD by
# condition, (c) records singularity and convergence for the primary fits,
# (d) refits the primary model leaving out each participant and each
# stimulus in turn and records the registered H1 contrast (human minus
# generator, averaged over image kind), and (e) refits with a
# condition-specific residual variance (nlme's varIdent, which gives each arm
# its own residual variance) so the heteroscedasticity finding has a
# model-based answer.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_diagnostics.pdf"),
              file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB,
                        c("study1_heteroscedasticity.csv",
                          "study1_lmm_convergence.csv",
                          "study1_influence_lopo.csv",
                          "study1_influence_loso.csv",
                          "study1_influence_summary.csv",
                          "study1_hetero_varident.csv")))

primary_fits <- list(creativity = creativity_res$fit, effort = effort_res$fit)
PRIMARY_CTRL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")   # identical to fit_primary_lmm()

# (a) Residual-vs-fitted plots and normal Q-Q plots (quantile-quantile plots,
# which set the residuals' distribution against a normal one), base
# graphics, one PDF.
pdf(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, "study1_diagnostics.pdf"), width = 8, height = 8)
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (dn in names(primary_fits)) {
  f  <- primary_fits[[dn]]
  fr <- f@frame
  r  <- residuals(f)
  plot(fitted(f), r, pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
       col = ifelse(fr$Type == "AI", "#3E3E3E80", "#A1A1A180"),
       xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual",
       main = paste0(stringr::str_to_title(dn), ": residuals vs fitted"))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  legend("topright", legend = c("Human", "AI"), pch = 16,
         col = c("#A1A1A1", "#3E3E3E"), bty = "n")
  qqnorm(r, pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
         main = paste0(stringr::str_to_title(dn), ": normal Q-Q of residuals"))
  qqline(r, lty = 2)
}
invisible(dev.off())   # suppress the device number dev.off() returns
# Also render inline for the HTML report.
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1))
for (dn in names(primary_fits)) {
  f <- primary_fits[[dn]]; r <- residuals(f)
  plot(fitted(f), r, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual",
       main = paste0(stringr::str_to_title(dn), ": residuals vs fitted"))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
  qqnorm(r, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, main = paste0(stringr::str_to_title(dn), ": Q-Q"))
  qqline(r, lty = 2)
}

# (b) Residual SD by Type and by stimulus_type, plus the participant-mean
# variance ratio the review reported. Both the residual (sigma) and the
# participant-level variance can differ by arm; the LMM assumes one of each.
hetero_table <- map_dfr(names(primary_fits), function(dn) {
  f  <- primary_fits[[dn]]
  fr <- f@frame %>% mutate(.resid = residuals(f))
  by_type <- fr %>% group_by(grp = paste0("Type=", Type)) %>%
    summarise(resid_sd = sd(.resid), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  by_stim <- fr %>% group_by(grp = paste0("stimulus_type=", stimulus_type)) %>%
    summarise(resid_sd = sd(.resid), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  pm <- fr %>% group_by(id, Type) %>% summarise(m = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")
  vt <- var.test(m ~ Type, data = pm)   # ratio Human/AI (factor order Human, AI)
  bind_rows(by_type, by_stim) %>%
    mutate(dimension = dn,
           resid_sd_ratio_AI_over_Human =
             by_type$resid_sd[by_type$grp == "Type=AI"] /
             by_type$resid_sd[by_type$grp == "Type=Human"],
           participant_mean_var_ratio_Human_over_AI = unname(vt$statistic),
           participant_mean_var_F_p = vt$p.value) %>%
    relocate(dimension)
})
hetero_table
write_csv(hetero_table, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_heteroscedasticity.csv"))
# Expected: effort residual SD ~0.66 (AI) vs ~0.84 (Human).
# Note the direction of the participant-mean column: it is var(Human) /
# var(AI) (var.test uses the factor order Human, AI), so an AI:Human
# variance ratio of 3.27 appears here as ~0.31 (effort, p ~ 2e-5;
# creativity ~0.54, p ~ .03). The two differences in spread run in opposite
# directions. The AI arm has smaller within-participant residual spread but
# larger between-participant spread of mean ratings, and the text must not
# collapse them into one "AI is more variable" sentence.
# Re-check these values on knit.

# (c) Singularity and convergence for the primary fits. converged requires
# both lmer_fit_status() (optimizer return code and lme4's check.conv
# messages, section 7) and performance::check_convergence(), which tests the
# scaled gradient at the solution against a tolerance of 0.001.
convergence_table <- map_dfr(names(primary_fits), function(dn) {
  f  <- primary_fits[[dn]]
  st <- lmer_fit_status(f)
  tibble(
    dimension    = dn,
    singular     = performance::check_singularity(f),
    converged    = st$converged && isTRUE(performance::check_convergence(f)),
    lme4_messages = st$lme4_messages,
    optimizer    = f@optinfo$optimizer
  )
})
convergence_table
stopifnot(!any(convergence_table$singular), all(convergence_table$converged))
write_csv(convergence_table, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_lmm_convergence.csv"))

# (d) Leave-one-participant-out (LOPO, 111 refits per dimension) and
# leave-one-stimulus-out (LOSO, 10 refits per dimension).
#
# What is recorded. The registered H1 contrast: the estimated marginal
# attribution contrast, human minus generator, averaged over the two image
# kinds with equal weight, in rating points (h1_contrast(), section 7). It is
# the quantity the confirmatory family in section 7.9 tests, so this check
# asks whether any single participant or image moves the headline number. It
# is not the TypeAI coefficient, which under treatment coding is the
# generator-minus-human difference at non-figurative images only. Positive
# values mean human-attributed work was rated higher.
#
# Weighting when an image is left out. Each image kind keeps equal weight:
# with one figurative image dropped, the figurative mean is taken over the
# remaining four and averaged with the non-figurative mean over five (and the
# reverse when a non-figurative image is dropped). That is how emmeans
# averages over stimulus_type, and it keeps the quantity the registered one.
#
# How. Each refit uses lme4::lmer with the primary model's formula and
# optimizer control. The contrast is read with asymptotic degrees of freedom,
# which skips the degrees-of-freedom computation on 242 refits; the estimate
# is the same under any method, and on the full-sample fits the standard
# error matches the Kenward-Roger one section 7.9 uses to ten decimals. No
# p-value is recorded. Each refit's convergence, singularity and
# error status is recorded (lmer_fit_status(), section 7), and a refit that
# errored or did not converge contributes no estimate: its estimate and
# standard error are NA and its note says why.
refit_h1 <- function(dat_sub) {
  warns <- character(0)
  f <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(
      lme4::lmer(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                 data = dat_sub, REML = TRUE, control = PRIMARY_CTRL),
      error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  status <- lmer_fit_status(f, warns)
  # emmeans notes on every call that Type is involved in an interaction,
  # which is why the contrast averages over image kind; the note is
  # silenced here so that it is not printed once per refit.
  h1 <- if (fit_usable(status)) suppressMessages(h1_contrast(f, "asymptotic"))
        else tibble(estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_)
  bind_cols(h1 %>% select(estimate, se), status) %>%
    mutate(note = fit_note(status, "estimate"))
}

influence_for <- function(dn, unit) {
  est_full <- h1_contrast(primary_fits[[dn]], "asymptotic")$estimate
  dsub <- long %>% filter(dimension == dn, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(Type          = relevel(factor(Type),          ref = "Human"),
           stimulus_type = relevel(factor(stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure"))
  units <- sort(unique(as.character(dsub[[unit]])))
  map_dfr(units, function(u) {
    out <- refit_h1(dsub %>% filter(.data[[unit]] != u) %>% droplevels())
    tibble(dimension = dn, unit = unit, dropped = u,
           estimate = out$estimate, se = out$se,
           est_full = est_full, delta = out$estimate - est_full,
           converged = out$converged, singular = out$singular,
           fit_error = out$fit_error, note = out$note,
           quantity = H1_CONTRAST_LABEL)
  })
}

influence_lopo <- bind_rows(influence_for("creativity", "id"),
                            influence_for("effort",     "id"))
influence_loso <- bind_rows(influence_for("creativity", "stimulus_id"),
                            influence_for("effort",     "stimulus_id"))
stopifnot(nrow(influence_lopo) == 2 * nrow(dat), nrow(influence_loso) == 20)
n_influence_unusable <- sum(is.na(influence_lopo$estimate)) +
                        sum(is.na(influence_loso$estimate))
cat("Leave-one-out refits that errored or did not converge:",
    n_influence_unusable, "of", nrow(influence_lopo) + nrow(influence_loso), "\n")

# The summary is over the usable refits only, and says how many those are.
influence_summary <- bind_rows(influence_lopo, influence_loso) %>%
  group_by(dimension, unit) %>%
  summarise(n_refits        = n(),
            n_refits_usable = sum(!is.na(estimate)),
            est_full        = first(est_full),
            min_est         = min(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_est         = max(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_abs_delta   = max(abs(delta), na.rm = TRUE),
            worst_case      = dropped[which.max(abs(delta))],
            all_same_sign   = all(sign(estimate) == sign(est_full), na.rm = TRUE),
            quantity        = first(quantity),
            .groups = "drop")
cat("\n=== Influence summary (H1 contrast, Human - AI averaged over image kind, under leave-one-out) ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(influence_summary %>% select(-quantity)))

write_csv(influence_lopo,    file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_influence_lopo.csv"))
write_csv(influence_loso,    file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_influence_loso.csv"))
write_csv(influence_summary, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_influence_summary.csv"))
# No single participant or stimulus should move the H1 contrast by more than
# ~0.1 rating points or flip its sign; if one does, name it in the supplement
# and re-run §10's forest plot with it highlighted.

# (e) Heteroscedasticity-robust refit: nlme::lme with a condition-specific
# residual variance (varIdent by Type), participant random intercept only
# (nlme cannot cross random effects cheaply; the stimulus intercept is
# omitted here, so compare against the same lme without varIdent, not
# against the crossed primary model). Skipped with a message if nlme is
# not installed; nlme is not attached with library() to avoid its masking
# of lme4 generics. Beside the coefficient rows, each model gets a row for
# the registered H1 contrast (human minus generator, averaged over image
# kind, read by emmeans), and est_primary_crossed_lmer on that row is the
# same contrast from the primary crossed model. nlme stops with an error
# when its optimizer does not converge, so a model that returns is a
# converged one; if either model stops, the whole refit is reported as
# skipped with the error message.
hetero_varident <- tryCatch({
  if (!requireNamespace("nlme", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("package nlme not installed; varIdent refit skipped")
  }
  map_dfr(names(primary_fits), function(dn) {
    dsub <- long %>% filter(dimension == dn, !is.na(rating)) %>%
      mutate(Type          = relevel(factor(Type),          ref = "Human"),
             stimulus_type = relevel(factor(stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure")) %>%
      as.data.frame()
    m_hom <- nlme::lme(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type, random = ~ 1 | id,
                       data = dsub, method = "REML")
    m_het <- nlme::lme(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type, random = ~ 1 | id,
                       weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Type),
                       data = dsub, method = "REML")
    var_ratio <- unname(coef(m_het$modelStruct$varStruct, unconstrained = FALSE))
    lrt <- anova(m_hom, m_het)
    h1_primary <- h1_contrast(primary_fits[[dn]])$estimate
    tidy_lme <- function(m, label) {
      tt <- summary(m)$tTable
      h1 <- h1_contrast(m, df_method = NULL)
      tibble(dimension = dn, model = label, term = rownames(tt),
             estimate = tt[, "Value"], se = tt[, "Std.Error"],
             df = tt[, "DF"], t = tt[, "t-value"], p = tt[, "p-value"],
             est_primary_crossed_lmer =
               unname(lme4::fixef(primary_fits[[dn]])[rownames(tt)])) %>%
        bind_rows(tibble(dimension = dn, model = label,
                         term = H1_CONTRAST_LABEL,
                         estimate = h1$estimate, se = h1$se, df = h1$df,
                         t = h1$estimate / h1$se, p = h1$p,
                         est_primary_crossed_lmer = h1_primary))
    }
    bind_rows(tidy_lme(m_hom, "lme homoscedastic (1|id)"),
              tidy_lme(m_het, "lme varIdent(~1|Type) (1|id)")) %>%
      mutate(varIdent_sd_ratio_AI_over_Human = var_ratio,
             lrt_varIdent_vs_hom_p = lrt$`p-value`[2]) %>%
      relocate(est_primary_crossed_lmer, .after = everything())
  })
}, error = function(e) {
  message("varIdent refit skipped: ", conditionMessage(e))
  tibble(dimension = NA_character_, model = "SKIPPED", term = NA_character_,
         note = conditionMessage(e))
})
hetero_varident
write_csv(hetero_varident, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_hetero_varident.csv"))
# Expected: the H1 contrast is unchanged under varIdent (it is a
# between-participant contrast; unequal residual variance mainly changes
# the SE), and the LRT, the likelihood-ratio test comparing the fit of the two
# models, favours varIdent for effort. The manuscript sentence is
# "estimates unchanged under a heteroscedastic refit".
# On these data the varIdent AI:Human SD ratio is above 1 in this lme (1.10
# creativity, 1.25 effort; LRT p = .035 / 9e-7), the opposite of the
# crossed-lmer residual pattern in (b) (AI:Human 0.93 / 0.78). This is not
# a contradiction. This lme has a single participant-intercept variance
# shared by both arms, so the AI arm's larger between-participant variance
# (see (b)) can only be absorbed by the AI residual stratum, and it
# outweighs the smaller within-participant spread. The H1 contrast (human
# minus generator, averaged over image kind) is identical under all three
# models (0.448 creativity, 0.921 effort), with SEs of 0.128-0.129
# (creativity) and 0.152-0.153 (effort). The arm-specific participant
# variance is modelled directly in section 7.8, where the registered test of
# H4 lives:
# `random = list(id = nlme::pdDiag(~ 0 + Type))` frees it, and freeing it is
# what lets the residual ratio there be read on its own terms rather than as
# the overflow of a between-participant difference with nowhere else to go.
```
