# 7.8 H4: what a rating is a property of (registered)

The three sections above ask how far the ratings move. This one asks what
they are a property of. Under human attribution a rating should mostly
track the particular artwork in front of the participant; under generator
attribution the prediction is that it mostly tracks the participant, who
applies one discount to whatever is shown. Written as variances, that is a
rise in the spread *between* participants together with a fall in the
spread *within* a participant from one image to the next.

The section runs in three parts: a descriptive partition of the rating
variance inside each arm, then the registered test, then two quantities
that make the same point without a model.

## 7.8.1 Variance partition (descriptive)

Inside one arm and one dimension, a model with no predictors and random
intercepts for participant and for image splits the total spread of the
ratings three ways: how much the images differ from each other, how much
the participants differ from each other, and the remainder: what is left
once both of those are taken out, the part specific to a particular person
seeing a particular image. The comparison that matters
is between arms, on the absolute variances; the proportions are printed
beside them and are description only, for the reason given in the code.

```{r h4-variance-partition}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# H4 says the attribution label changes what a rating is a property of. Under
# human attribution a rating should mostly track the particular artwork being
# judged; under generator attribution it should mostly track the particular
# person judging, who applies one discount to whatever is shown. In variance
# terms, the variance between participants rises and the variance within a
# participant from image to image falls.
#
# The section has three parts, in order:
#   (i)   a descriptive three-way partition of the rating variance inside each
#         arm, so the reader can see where the variance sits before any test;
#   (ii)  the registered test, two fits per dimension with different
#         covariance structures: an lme4 fit in which the
#         between-participant variance is free to differ by arm, and an nlme
#         fit in which the residual variance is free to differ by arm, with a
#         likelihood-ratio test for each; and
#   (iii) two descriptive quantities that say the same thing without a model.
#
# Terms used below:
#   variance component     the part of the spread in the ratings attributable
#                          to one source (images, participants, or what is left
#                          over), estimated by the mixed model rather than
#                          computed directly.
#   likelihood-ratio test  a comparison of two nested models by twice the
#                          difference in their log-likelihoods, referred to a
#                          chi-square distribution with degrees of freedom
#                          equal to the difference in the number of parameters.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

H4_CTRL <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_partition.csv"))

# --- (i) Variance partition -------------------------------------------------
#
# Within one arm and one dimension, an intercept-only crossed model
#
#     rating ~ 1 + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
#
# splits the total spread of the ratings into three parts: how much images
# differ from each other on average, how much participants differ from each
# other on average, and the remainder, which is the part specific to a
# particular person seeing a particular image (it also carries any measurement
# noise, because each person rates each image once and the two cannot be
# separated with a single observation per cell).
#
# There are no fixed effects here on purpose. Adding stimulus_type would move
# the between-image differences it explains out of the image component and into
# the fixed part, which is not what a partition of the observed spread should
# do. Each arm is fitted separately because the whole question is whether the
# partition differs between them; a pooled fit would impose one answer.
#
# How to read the output. Compare the absolute variances across arms, in the
# column `variance`. The `proportion` column is compositional: the three
# shares are divided by their own total and so must sum to one. No component
# can rise without another falling, and a proportion can move purely because
# a different component moved. The registered claim in H4 is about the
# absolute variances; the proportions are reported as description only and
# carry no verdict.

variance_partition_for <- function(dim_name, type_name, data = long) {

  dsub <- data %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, Type == type_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    droplevels()

  components <- c("between images", "between participants",
                  "person-by-image remainder")

  fit <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(rating ~ 1 + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
               data = dsub, REML = TRUE, control = H4_CTRL),
    error = function(e) e)

  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    message("Variance partition failed for ", dim_name, " / ", type_name,
            ": ", conditionMessage(fit))
    return(tibble(dimension = dim_name, Type = type_name,
                  component = components, variance = NA_real_, sd = NA_real_,
                  proportion = NA_real_,
                  n_participants = n_distinct(dsub$id), n_ratings = nrow(dsub),
                  singular = NA,
                  note = paste("fit failed:", conditionMessage(fit)),
                  converged = FALSE,
                  lme4_messages = conditionMessage(fit)))
  }

  vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(fit))
  pick <- function(g) vc$vcov[vc$grp == g][1]
  v <- c(pick("stimulus_id"), pick("id"), pick("Residual"))
  status <- lmer_fit_status(fit)

  tibble(dimension = dim_name, Type = type_name, component = components,
         variance = v, sd = sqrt(v), proportion = v / sum(v),
         n_participants = n_distinct(dsub$id), n_ratings = nrow(dsub),
         singular = status$singular,
         note = if (status$converged) ""
                else paste("fit did not converge:", status$lme4_messages),
         converged = status$converged,
         lme4_messages = status$lme4_messages)
}

h4_grid <- expand_grid(dimension = DIM_LEVELS, Type = TYPE_LEVELS)
h4_variance_partition <- map2_dfr(h4_grid$dimension, h4_grid$Type,
                                  variance_partition_for)

cat("=== H4 (i): variance partition within each arm and dimension ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h4_variance_partition %>%
                      mutate(across(c(variance, sd, proportion), ~ round(.x, 4)))))

write_csv(h4_variance_partition,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_partition.csv"))
```

## 7.8.2 The registered test

Two variances estimated in two separate models cannot be compared, because
nothing in either model supplies a standard error for their difference.
The registered test therefore puts both arms in one model and lets the
between-participant variance take a different value in each, then asks by
a likelihood-ratio test whether that freedom earns its extra parameter.
The prediction is a conjunction: the between-participant variance rises
*and* the image-to-image remainder falls. The residual variance is
therefore freed by arm as well, in a second fit, and reported beside the
first. The two fits do not share one covariance structure. The
between-participant fit keeps a random intercept for each image but holds
one residual variance for both arms; the residual fit lets the residual
variance differ by arm but has no image intercept, so its residual also
carries the differences between images. The two ratios are read from those
two fits, and the table says which fit each comes from. The support
criterion is stated on the two variance ratios, not on the tests. Each ratio
is reported with a 95 percent confidence interval from a bootstrap, which
re-estimates the ratio on many data sets resampled from the participants
within each arm. H4 is claimed on a dimension only if the between-participant
ratio is above 1 with its whole interval above 1, and the residual ratio is
below 1 with its whole interval below 1.

```{r h4-variance-test}
# --- (ii) The registered test ----------------------------------------------
#
# Bootstrap settings for the confidence intervals on the two variance ratios;
# the resampling itself is explained and run further down this chunk. B_H4 is
# the number of resamples per dimension. Each resample refits the lme4 model
# and the nlme model once, at roughly a twentieth of a second for the pair, so
# the full run takes about a minute and a half for both dimensions together;
# a slower machine may need a few minutes. H4_BOOT_SEED is the file's seed
# constant, the same value set.seed() takes in section 1.1 and the registered
# effect size uses in section 9.1; it is reset before each dimension so that
# either dimension's interval can be reproduced on its own and, because the
# two dimensions share the same participants, the same participants are drawn
# on both.
B_H4         <- 1000L
H4_BOOT_SEED <- 20260421L
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_test.csv"))

# The covariance structure behind each ratio, written into the table so the
# two ratios are never read as coming from one model (explained below under
# "Two covariance structures, not one model").
H4_BETWEEN_MODEL  <- paste0(
  "lme4: participant intercept variance by arm, one residual variance shared ",
  "by both arms, image random intercept")
H4_RESIDUAL_MODEL <- paste0(
  "nlme: participant intercept variance by arm, residual variance by arm ",
  "(varIdent), no image random intercept")

# The partition above fits each arm separately, which is fine for description
# but gives no test: two numbers estimated in two models cannot be compared
# without a standard error for their difference. The registered test therefore
# fits both arms in one model and lets the between-participant variance take a
# different value in each, then asks whether that freedom buys enough fit to be
# worth its extra parameter.
#
# Arm-specific random effects. Two indicator columns are created:
# Human_indicator is 1 for a row from the human arm and 0 otherwise, and
# AI_indicator is the reverse. The participant random effect is then
# written as
#
#     (0 + Human_indicator | id) + (0 + AI_indicator | id)
#
# The leading 0 suppresses the usual random intercept, so each term is a random
# slope on its indicator with no intercept of its own. Because attribution is
# between-participant, every row belonging to one person carries the same pair
# of indicator values: for a person in the human arm, Human_indicator is 1
# throughout, so the first term acts as that person's intercept, and
# AI_indicator is 0 throughout, so the second term multiplies by zero and
# contributes nothing at all. The reverse holds for a person in the generator
# arm. The result is one random intercept per participant, drawn from a
# distribution whose variance depends on which arm the participant is in, and
# lme4 estimates the two variances in a single fit. Writing the two terms as
# separate bars is what forces them to be independent; a single
# `(0 + Type | id)` bar would additionally try to estimate a correlation
# between two effects that are never both active for the same person.
#
# The comparison model is the primary structure, `(1 | id)`, which holds one
# between-participant variance common to both arms. The two models have
# identical fixed effects and differ by exactly one variance parameter, so they
# are compared by a likelihood-ratio test on 1 degree of freedom, computed on
# the restricted-maximum-likelihood fits (refit = FALSE). Restricted maximum
# likelihood is the fitting method used throughout this file, the `REML = TRUE`
# argument on every lmer call above: it estimates the variance components after
# removing the part of the data the fixed effects explain, so those effects
# cannot absorb spread that belongs to the participants or the images. That is
# what makes it the right likelihood to compare on when the two models
# differ only in their random effects and share their fixed effects, as these
# two do; had the fixed effects differed, the comparison would have to be
# refitted by ordinary maximum likelihood instead.
#
# Which reference distribution. The parameter space is the set of values the
# model's parameters are allowed to take; for a variance that is zero and
# everything above it. A null hypothesis sits at an interior point of that
# space when the values it fixes can be moved a little in every direction and
# still be allowed values, and at a boundary point when they can be moved in
# one direction only. Testing a variance against zero puts the null on the
# boundary: a variance can be raised from zero but not lowered below it, so
# the estimate can only ever land on one side of the null, and the ordinary
# chi-square is the wrong reference; the corrected one is a fifty-fifty
# mixture of a chi-square on zero degrees of freedom (a spike at zero) and a
# chi-square on one degree of freedom. That is not the situation here. The
# null equates the two between-participant variances at a common positive
# value, and from that point either variance can be nudged up or down and
# still be a valid variance, so the null is an interior point, the
# likelihood-ratio statistic behaves as it does in any ordinary nested
# comparison, and the ordinary chi-square on 1 degree of freedom is the
# correct reference. That is what the p-value below uses, and the output
# records it in the `lrt_between_reference` column. The residual comparison
# further down is the same: its null equates two positive residual variances
# at a common value, again an interior point, so it also uses the ordinary
# chi-square on 1 degree of freedom, and the output records that in the
# `lrt_residual_reference` column beside its p-value.
#
# The residual half. H4 is a conjunction. It predicts a rise in the
# between-participant variance and a fall in the within-participant,
# image-to-image variance, so the residual variance has to be freed by arm as
# well. lme4 fits a single residual variance and cannot free it, so this half
# is fitted with nlme::lme, whose `weights = varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Type)`
# argument gives each arm its own residual variance. To keep the two halves of
# the conjunction from being confounded, that fit also frees the
# between-participant variance by arm, using
# `random = list(id = pdDiag(~ 0 + Type))`, which is the same indicator trick
# in nlme's notation (pdDiag means the two variances are estimated with no
# correlation between them). Without the arm-specific participant variance, a
# larger between-participant spread in one arm has nowhere to go but that
# arm's residual, and the residual ratio would report the opposite of what it
# should.
#
# nlme is called with :: rather than attached, because attaching it masks lme4
# generics that later chunks rely on.
#
# Two covariance structures, not one model. The two registered ratios come
# from two different fits, and the fits differ in more than which variance
# they free:
#   between-participant ratio  lme4 fit: participant intercept variance free
#                              by arm, one residual variance shared by both
#                              arms, and a random intercept for each image.
#   residual ratio             nlme fit: participant intercept variance free
#                              by arm, residual variance free by arm, and no
#                              image random intercept, because nlme cannot
#                              cross two random effects cheaply.
# Neither fit is the primary model of sections 7.1 and 7.2, and they are not
# one model. Two consequences follow. First, the lme4 fit holds the residual
# variance equal across arms, which is the very thing the second half of H4
# predicts is false; its between-participant ratio is estimated under that
# constraint. Second, the nlme fit's residual stratum holds the differences
# between images as well as the person-by-image remainder. The partition in
# 7.8.1 shows how much that second point matters. On effort the between-image
# variance is nearly the same in the two arms (about 0.093 human and 0.089
# generator), so the arm difference in the residual stratum comes from the
# remainder, the component H4 speaks about. On creativity it is smaller in
# the generator arm (about 0.17 against 0.25), and that difference adds to
# the residual stratum's arm difference in the predicted direction. The table
# names the fit behind each ratio in `between_ratio_model` and
# `residual_ratio_model`.
#
# How to read the output. `var_between_AI` above `var_between_Human`, so a
# `ratio_between_AI_over_Human` above 1, is the first half of H4;
# `ratio_residual_AI_over_Human` below 1 is the second. H4 needs both. The
# likelihood-ratio p-values say whether each freed variance earns its
# parameter; the registered verdict rests on the confidence intervals around
# the two ratios, which are computed below by resampling participants and
# carried in the same table. Each fit's convergence status is carried too: a
# likelihood-ratio p-value from a fit that errored or did not converge is set
# to NA, and so is the verdict that depends on it.

h4_variance_test_for <- function(dim_name, data = long) {

  dsub <- data %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    droplevels() %>%
    mutate(Type            = relevel(factor(Type),          ref = "Human"),
           stimulus_type   = relevel(factor(stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure"),
           Human_indicator = as.numeric(Type == "Human"),
           AI_indicator    = as.numeric(Type == "AI"))

  # --- between-participant half, in lme4 ---
  fit_common <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
               data = dsub, REML = TRUE, control = H4_CTRL),
    error = function(e) e)
  fit_byarm <- tryCatch(
    lme4::lmer(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type +
                 (0 + Human_indicator | id) + (0 + AI_indicator | id) +
                 (1 | stimulus_id),
               data = dsub, REML = TRUE, control = H4_CTRL),
    error = function(e) e)

  # Both lme4 fits enter the likelihood-ratio test, so the between half is
  # usable only if both converged.
  st_common <- lmer_fit_status(fit_common)
  st_byarm  <- lmer_fit_status(fit_byarm)
  between_converged <- fit_usable(st_common) && fit_usable(st_byarm)
  between_messages  <- paste(c(paste("common:", st_common$lme4_messages),
                               paste("by arm:", st_byarm$lme4_messages)),
                             collapse = " | ")

  between <- list(v_human = NA_real_, v_ai = NA_real_, chisq = NA_real_,
                  df = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, singular = NA,
                  note = "")
  if (inherits(fit_common, "error") || inherits(fit_byarm, "error")) {
    failed <- if (inherits(fit_byarm, "error")) fit_byarm else fit_common
    between$note <- paste("between-participant fit failed:",
                          conditionMessage(failed))
    message("H4 between-participant test failed for ", dim_name, ": ",
            between$note)
  } else {
    vc <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(fit_byarm))
    between$v_human <- vc$vcov[which(vc$var1 == "Human_indicator")][1]
    between$v_ai    <- vc$vcov[which(vc$var1 == "AI_indicator")][1]
    lrt <- tryCatch(anova(fit_common, fit_byarm, refit = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) e)
    if (inherits(lrt, "error")) {
      between$note <- paste("likelihood-ratio test failed:",
                            conditionMessage(lrt))
      message("H4 likelihood-ratio test failed for ", dim_name, ": ",
              between$note)
    } else {
      between$chisq <- lrt$Chisq[2]
      between$df    <- lrt$Df[2]
      between$p     <- if (between_converged) lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] else NA_real_
    }
    between$singular <- lme4::isSingular(fit_byarm, tol = 1e-4)
    if (!between_converged) {
      between$note <- paste("a between-participant fit did not converge, so",
                            "the likelihood-ratio p-value and the verdict are",
                            "set to NA:", between_messages)
    }
  }

  # --- residual half, in nlme, with the participant variance also freed ---
  residual <- list(v_human = NA_real_, v_ai = NA_real_, chisq = NA_real_,
                   df = NA_real_, p = NA_real_,
                   v_between_human = NA_real_, v_between_ai = NA_real_,
                   note = "")
  res_try <- tryCatch({
    if (!requireNamespace("nlme", quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop("package nlme not installed; the residual half of H4 cannot be fitted")
    }
    dnl <- as.data.frame(dsub)
    m_one_resid <- nlme::lme(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type,
                             random = list(id = nlme::pdDiag(~ 0 + Type)),
                             data = dnl, method = "REML")
    m_two_resid <- nlme::lme(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type,
                             random  = list(id = nlme::pdDiag(~ 0 + Type)),
                             weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Type),
                             data = dnl, method = "REML")
    lrt_r <- anova(m_one_resid, m_two_resid)
    # varIdent reports each arm's residual standard deviation as a multiple of
    # a reference stratum whose multiplier is fixed at 1; nlme chooses that
    # reference from the order the strata appear in the data, so the arm it
    # picks is not fixed in advance. Asking for allCoef = TRUE returns the
    # multiplier for both arms, named, including the reference's 1, and
    # sigma is the reference arm's residual standard deviation. Each arm's
    # residual variance is therefore (sigma * multiplier)^2, read out by name
    # rather than by position.
    vmult <- coef(m_two_resid$modelStruct$varStruct,
                  unconstrained = FALSE, allCoef = TRUE)
    stopifnot(all(TYPE_LEVELS %in% names(vmult)))
    sigma_ref <- m_two_resid$sigma
    # nlme::VarCorr returns a character matrix; the two participant variances
    # sit in the "Variance" column, one row per Type level.
    vcn <- suppressWarnings(nlme::VarCorr(m_two_resid))
    v_between <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(vcn[, "Variance"]))
    names(v_between) <- rownames(vcn)
    # nlme::lme() stops with an error when its optimizer does not converge
    # (lmeControl's returnObject is FALSE by default), so two fits that
    # return here are two converged fits.
    list(v_human = (sigma_ref * vmult[["Human"]])^2,
         v_ai    = (sigma_ref * vmult[["AI"]])^2,
         chisq = lrt_r$L.Ratio[2], df = lrt_r$df[2] - lrt_r$df[1],
         p = lrt_r$`p-value`[2],
         v_between_human = unname(v_between["TypeHuman"]),
         v_between_ai    = unname(v_between["TypeAI"]),
         converged = TRUE, error_message = "",
         note = "")
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("H4 residual test failed for ", dim_name, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
    list(v_human = NA_real_, v_ai = NA_real_, chisq = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
         p = NA_real_, v_between_human = NA_real_, v_between_ai = NA_real_,
         converged = FALSE, error_message = conditionMessage(e),
         note = paste("residual fit failed or did not converge:",
                      conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  residual <- res_try

  tibble(
    dimension                    = dim_name,
    var_between_Human            = between$v_human,
    var_between_AI               = between$v_ai,
    ratio_between_AI_over_Human  = between$v_ai / between$v_human,
    lrt_between_chisq            = between$chisq,
    lrt_between_df               = between$df,
    lrt_between_p                = between$p,
    lrt_between_reference        = "chi-square (interior null: two positive variances set equal)",
    byarm_fit_singular           = between$singular,
    var_residual_Human           = residual$v_human,
    var_residual_AI              = residual$v_ai,
    ratio_residual_AI_over_Human = residual$v_ai / residual$v_human,
    lrt_residual_chisq           = residual$chisq,
    lrt_residual_df              = residual$df,
    lrt_residual_p               = residual$p,
    lrt_residual_reference       = "chi-square (interior null: two positive residual variances set equal)",
    nlme_var_between_Human       = residual$v_between_human,
    nlme_var_between_AI          = residual$v_between_ai,
    h4_direction_met             = isTRUE(between$v_ai > between$v_human) &&
                                   isTRUE(residual$v_ai < residual$v_human),
    note                         = paste(c(between$note, residual$note),
                                         collapse = " "),
    between_fit_converged        = between_converged,
    between_fit_error            = st_common$fit_error || st_byarm$fit_error,
    between_fit_messages         = between_messages,
    residual_fit_converged       = residual$converged,
    residual_fit_error           = !residual$converged,
    residual_fit_messages        = residual$error_message,
    between_ratio_model          = H4_BETWEEN_MODEL,
    residual_ratio_model         = H4_RESIDUAL_MODEL
  )
}

h4_variance_test <- map_dfr(DIM_LEVELS, h4_variance_test_for)

cat("\n=== H4 (ii): registered variance test, two fits per dimension ===\n")
cat("Between-participant ratio from:", H4_BETWEEN_MODEL, "\n")
cat("Residual ratio from:           ", H4_RESIDUAL_MODEL, "\n")
print(as.data.frame(h4_variance_test %>%
  select(dimension, var_between_Human, var_between_AI,
         ratio_between_AI_over_Human, lrt_between_chisq, lrt_between_df,
         lrt_between_p) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
print(as.data.frame(h4_variance_test %>%
  select(dimension, var_residual_Human, var_residual_AI,
         ratio_residual_AI_over_Human, lrt_residual_chisq, lrt_residual_df,
         lrt_residual_p, nlme_var_between_Human, nlme_var_between_AI,
         h4_direction_met) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

# --- The registered confidence intervals, by participant bootstrap ----------
#
# The likelihood-ratio tests above say whether freeing each variance by arm
# improves the fit. The registered support criterion for H4 is stated on the
# ratios themselves, and it asks for a confidence interval around each. A
# bootstrap is a way of getting an interval without a formula for the standard
# error: the data are resampled many times, the quantity of interest is
# recomputed on each resample, and the spread of those recomputed values
# stands in for the sampling variation of the original. The percentile
# interval is the simplest version of it: the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of
# the resampled values are taken as the 95 percent interval.
#
# What is resampled, and why. The participant is the sampled unit in this
# design: the ten images are the fixed set every participant saw, and H4 is
# a claim about how ratings vary across people. Each resample therefore draws
# participants, with replacement, and carries each drawn participant's ten
# ratings along as a block. Drawing within each arm separately (a stratified
# resample) keeps every resample at 56 human-arm and 55 generator-arm
# participants, so the arm sizes never vary from the observed design. A
# participant drawn twice appears twice, and each copy is given its own
# participant label, because a random-effects model reads the label as the
# unit: two blocks of ten rows sharing one label would be fitted as a single
# participant with twenty ratings, which is not what a repeated draw means.
#
# Both models are refitted on every resample, the lme4 model with the
# arm-specific between-participant variances and the nlme model with the
# arm-specific residual variances, and the two ratios are recomputed on the
# same draw. A resample whose refit stops with an error contributes nothing
# and is counted. A resample whose lme4 refit is singular, meaning that at
# least one of its variances sits at zero, the boundary of its range (this
# model has no correlations, so a variance is the only thing that can reach
# a boundary), is a legitimate estimate at the edge of the range: it is kept
# when its ratio is finite, and its count is reported beside the failures. A
# ratio that is not finite is unusable as a number: a human-arm variance of
# exactly zero makes the between-participant ratio infinite, or undefined
# when both variances are zero. Such a resample is counted with the failures
# in `n_boot_failed_between` (and likewise in `n_boot_failed_residual`) even
# though the refit itself did not stop. A
# resample whose lme4 refit may not have converged (the optimizer returned a
# non-zero code, or the refit raised a warning, which is how lme4 reports a
# failed convergence check) is also unusable and is counted with the
# failures, and the number of such refits is reported on its own in
# `n_boot_warning_between`. The failure counts are therefore counts of
# resamples that yielded no usable ratio, whatever the reason. lme4 warnings
# about convergence are muffled inside the loop, because a thousand of them
# would bury the output, and counted instead. lme4 reports a singular fit as a
# message rather than a warning, so those notices are silenced separately with
# suppressMessages(); the singular count comes from isSingular() on each
# refit, not from the notice. The nlme refit stops with an error when it does
# not converge, so a residual ratio is recorded only from a converged refit.
#
# The support criterion, as registered: H4 is supported on a dimension only if
# the between-participant ratio is above 1 and the residual ratio is below 1
# and each interval excludes 1, meaning the whole interval lies on one side of
# it. The interval is checked on the predicted side directly: the lower end of
# the between-participant interval above 1, and the upper end of the residual
# interval below 1. The `h4_supported` column is that conjunction and nothing
# weaker. It is NA, not FALSE, when either half's fits errored or did not
# converge, because no verdict can then be read.

h4_bootstrap_for <- function(dim_name, data = long, B = B_H4,
                             seed = H4_BOOT_SEED) {

  dsub <- data %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    droplevels() %>%
    mutate(Type          = relevel(factor(Type),          ref = "Human"),
           stimulus_type = relevel(factor(stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure"),
           id            = as.character(id))

  # Which participants belong to which arm, and which rows each participant
  # owns, computed once so the loop only has to index.
  id_arm     <- dsub %>% distinct(id, Type)
  arm_ids    <- split(id_arm$id, id_arm$Type)
  rows_by_id <- split(seq_len(nrow(dsub)), dsub$id)
  stopifnot(all(TYPE_LEVELS %in% names(arm_ids)))

  ratio_between    <- rep(NA_real_, B)
  ratio_residual   <- rep(NA_real_, B)
  singular_between <- rep(NA, B)
  warned_between   <- rep(FALSE, B)

  set.seed(seed)
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {

    # Stratified draw: each arm's participants resampled with replacement,
    # keeping the arm sizes; every copy of a participant gets its own label.
    draw  <- unlist(lapply(arm_ids, function(ids)
                      sample(ids, length(ids), replace = TRUE)),
                    use.names = FALSE)
    idx   <- unlist(rows_by_id[draw], use.names = FALSE)
    dboot <- dsub[idx, ]
    dboot$id <- factor(rep(seq_along(draw),
                           times = lengths(rows_by_id[draw])))
    dboot$Human_indicator <- as.numeric(dboot$Type == "Human")
    dboot$AI_indicator    <- as.numeric(dboot$Type == "AI")

    # Between-participant half: the same lme4 model as above, refitted.
    fit_b <- withCallingHandlers(
      tryCatch(
        suppressMessages(
          lme4::lmer(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type +
                       (0 + Human_indicator | id) + (0 + AI_indicator | id) +
                       (1 | stimulus_id),
                     data = dboot, REML = TRUE, control = H4_CTRL)),
        error = function(e) e),
      warning = function(w) {
        warned_between[b] <<- TRUE
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      })
    if (!inherits(fit_b, "error")) {
      # A non-zero optimizer code is a non-converged fit even if no warning
      # was raised.
      if (!isTRUE(all(fit_b@optinfo$conv$opt == 0))) warned_between[b] <- TRUE
      vc  <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(fit_b))
      v_h <- vc$vcov[which(vc$var1 == "Human_indicator")][1]
      v_a <- vc$vcov[which(vc$var1 == "AI_indicator")][1]
      r   <- v_a / v_h
      ratio_between[b]    <- if (is.finite(r) && !warned_between[b]) r
                             else NA_real_
      singular_between[b] <- lme4::isSingular(fit_b, tol = 1e-4)
    }

    # Residual half: the same nlme model as above, refitted. Only the varIdent
    # multipliers are needed here: each arm's residual variance is (sigma times
    # its multiplier) squared, so sigma cancels out of the ratio.
    fit_r <- tryCatch(
      suppressWarnings(
        nlme::lme(rating ~ Type * stimulus_type,
                  random  = list(id = nlme::pdDiag(~ 0 + Type)),
                  weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Type),
                  data = as.data.frame(dboot), method = "REML")),
      error = function(e) e)
    if (!inherits(fit_r, "error")) {
      vmult <- coef(fit_r$modelStruct$varStruct,
                    unconstrained = FALSE, allCoef = TRUE)
      if (all(TYPE_LEVELS %in% names(vmult))) {
        r <- (vmult[["AI"]] / vmult[["Human"]])^2
        ratio_residual[b] <- if (is.finite(r)) r else NA_real_
      }
    }
  }

  ci_b <- unname(quantile(ratio_between,  c(0.025, 0.975), type = 7,
                          na.rm = TRUE))
  ci_r <- unname(quantile(ratio_residual, c(0.025, 0.975), type = 7,
                          na.rm = TRUE))

  tibble(dimension               = dim_name,
         ci_low_between          = ci_b[1],
         ci_high_between         = ci_b[2],
         ci_low_residual         = ci_r[1],
         ci_high_residual        = ci_r[2],
         n_boot                  = B,
         n_boot_failed_between   = sum(is.na(ratio_between)),
         n_boot_failed_residual  = sum(is.na(ratio_residual)),
         n_boot_singular_between = sum(singular_between, na.rm = TRUE),
         n_boot_warning_between  = sum(warned_between),
         boot_seed               = seed)
}

h4_bootstrap <- map_dfr(DIM_LEVELS, h4_bootstrap_for)

# Join the intervals onto the test table, then apply the registered criterion.
# "Excludes 1" is read literally and on the predicted side: the whole
# between-participant interval above 1, the whole residual interval below 1.
# A dimension whose fits errored or did not converge gets NA; a missing
# interval with usable fits counts as not meeting the criterion.
# h4_supported_both_dimensions is the H4 conjunction across the two
# dimensions, repeated on both rows: TRUE only if both dimensions are TRUE,
# FALSE if either is FALSE, and NA otherwise.
h4_variance_test <- h4_variance_test %>%
  left_join(h4_bootstrap, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(h4_supported = if_else(
    between_fit_converged & residual_fit_converged,
    coalesce(ratio_between_AI_over_Human > 1 & ci_low_between > 1 &
               ratio_residual_AI_over_Human < 1 & ci_high_residual < 1,
             FALSE),
    NA)) %>%
  mutate(h4_supported_both_dimensions =
           if (any(h4_supported %in% FALSE)) FALSE
           else if (anyNA(h4_supported)) NA
           else TRUE)

cat("\n=== H4 (ii): participant-bootstrap intervals on the two ratios ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h4_variance_test %>%
  select(dimension, ratio_between_AI_over_Human, ci_low_between,
         ci_high_between, ratio_residual_AI_over_Human, ci_low_residual,
         ci_high_residual, n_boot, n_boot_failed_between,
         n_boot_failed_residual, n_boot_singular_between,
         n_boot_warning_between, h4_supported) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

# The registered verdict in words, one dimension at a time and never averaged
# across them.
for (dn in DIM_LEVELS) {
  row <- h4_variance_test %>% filter(dimension == dn)
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "\nH4, %s: the between-participant variance ratio (generator over human) ",
    "is %.2f, 95 percent bootstrap interval [%.2f, %.2f]; the residual ",
    "variance ratio is %.2f, interval [%.2f, %.2f]. The registered criterion ",
    "(first ratio above 1, second below 1, both intervals excluding 1) is ",
    "%s. (%d resamples; %d between-participant refits failed and %d were ",
    "singular; %d residual refits failed.)\n"),
    dn, row$ratio_between_AI_over_Human, row$ci_low_between,
    row$ci_high_between, row$ratio_residual_AI_over_Human,
    row$ci_low_residual, row$ci_high_residual,
    if (is.na(row$h4_supported)) {
      "unavailable, because a fit behind it errored or did not converge"
    } else if (row$h4_supported) {
      "met, so H4 is supported on this dimension"
    } else "not met, so H4 is not supported on this dimension",
    row$n_boot, row$n_boot_failed_between, row$n_boot_singular_between,
    row$n_boot_failed_residual))
}
both_h4 <- h4_variance_test$h4_supported_both_dimensions[1]
cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "\nH4 across both dimensions, the registered conjunction: %s. This ",
  "criterion, and not the likelihood-ratio p-value that enters the Holm ",
  "family in section 7.9, decides H4.\n"),
  if (is.na(both_h4)) "unavailable" else if (both_h4) "met" else "not met"))

write_csv(h4_variance_test,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_variance_test.csv"))
```

## 7.8.3 Descriptive support

Two quantities a reader can check against the raw ratings: how many
participants gave the same rating to at least seven of the ten artworks,
and how tightly the ten ratings hang together within each arm. Neither
decides H4; both should move in the same direction as the test if the
account behind H4 is right.

```{r h4-descriptive}
# --- (iii) Descriptive support ----------------------------------------------
#
# Two quantities that make the same point without a model, and that a reader
# can check against the raw ratings. Neither is part of the support criterion
# for H4; both are description.
#
# Flat responding. For each participant and dimension we take the ten ratings
# and count how many fall on the single most-used value, then record whether
# that count reaches seven. A participant who gave the same rating to seven or
# more of the ten artworks was, on that dimension, barely distinguishing the
# artworks at all. If attribution to a generator turns rating into a property
# of the rater, that proportion should be higher in the generator arm.
#
# Internal consistency. Cronbach's alpha treats the ten artworks as ten items
# of one scale and reports how much the ratings hang together across them. It
# rises when participants keep their relative positions from image to image,
# which is the between-participant consistency H4 predicts will increase.
# It is computed inside each arm separately, because computing it across both
# arms at once would count the attribution effect itself as consistency
# between people and inflate the number.
#
# psych is called with :: rather than attached, because psych::alpha masks
# ggplot2::alpha, which the figure chunks use.
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_descriptive.csv"))

alpha_within_arm <- function(dim_name, type_name, data = long) {
  tryCatch({
    if (!requireNamespace("psych", quietly = TRUE)) {
      stop("package psych not installed")
    }
    mat <- data %>%
      filter(dimension == dim_name, Type == type_name) %>%
      select(id, stimulus_id, rating) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = stimulus_id, values_from = rating) %>%
      select(-id) %>%
      as.matrix()
    stopifnot(ncol(mat) == 10, nrow(mat) > 2)
    suppressMessages(psych::alpha(mat, check.keys = FALSE)$total$raw_alpha)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Cronbach's alpha failed for ", dim_name, " / ", type_name, ": ",
            conditionMessage(e))
    NA_real_
  })
}

flat_responding <- long %>%
  filter(!is.na(rating)) %>%
  group_by(Type, dimension, id) %>%
  summarise(n_rated  = n(),
            max_same = max(table(rating)),   # size of the largest tied block
            .groups  = "drop") %>%
  mutate(same_on_7_or_more = max_same >= 7) %>%
  group_by(Type, dimension) %>%
  summarise(n_participants        = n(),
            n_same_on_7_or_more   = sum(same_on_7_or_more),
            prop_same_on_7_or_more = mean(same_on_7_or_more),
            median_largest_block  = median(max_same),
            .groups = "drop")

h4_descriptive <- flat_responding %>%
  mutate(cronbach_alpha_within_arm =
           map2_dbl(as.character(dimension), as.character(Type),
                    ~ alpha_within_arm(.x, .y))) %>%
  arrange(dimension, Type)

cat("\n=== H4 (iii): descriptive support ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h4_descriptive %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))))

write_csv(h4_descriptive,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h4_descriptive.csv"))

# A compact statement of the registered conclusion, printed so the reader does
# not have to assemble it from three tables. H4 asks for a rise in the
# between-participant variance and a fall in the residual variance on the same
# dimension; it is reported per dimension and never averaged across them. The
# bracketed values beside each ratio are its 95 percent bootstrap interval
# from section 7.8.2, and the final clause is the registered criterion read
# off the `h4_supported` column.
for (dn in DIM_LEVELS) {
  row <- h4_variance_test %>% filter(dimension == dn)
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("\nH4, %s: between-participant variance %.3f (human) vs %.3f ",
           "(generator), ratio %.2f [%.2f, %.2f], chi-square(%s) = %.2f, ",
           "p = %.3g; residual variance %.3f vs %.3f, ratio %.2f [%.2f, %.2f], ",
           "chi-square(%s) = %.2f, p = %.3g. Predicted direction on both ",
           "components: %s. Registered criterion, ratios on the predicted ",
           "sides of 1 with both intervals excluding 1: %s.\n"),
    dn, row$var_between_Human, row$var_between_AI,
    row$ratio_between_AI_over_Human, row$ci_low_between, row$ci_high_between,
    format(row$lrt_between_df),
    row$lrt_between_chisq, row$lrt_between_p,
    row$var_residual_Human, row$var_residual_AI,
    row$ratio_residual_AI_over_Human, row$ci_low_residual, row$ci_high_residual,
    format(row$lrt_residual_df),
    row$lrt_residual_chisq, row$lrt_residual_p,
    ifelse(isTRUE(row$h4_direction_met), "yes", "no"),
    if (is.na(row$h4_supported)) "unavailable"
    else if (row$h4_supported) "met" else "not met"))
}
```

# 7.9 Multiplicity across the confirmatory family (registered)

Four tests carry the confirmatory claims: the attribution contrast on
creativity, the attribution contrast on effort, the attribution-by-dimension
term from the joint model, and the likelihood-ratio test on the
between-participant variance. Running four tests at .05 each gives roughly a
one-in-five chance that at least one comes out significant when nothing is
there, so they are corrected together by the Holm procedure at a family-wise
alpha of .05. The family is exactly these four, as section 7 of the
registration lists them. That list and the choice of the Holm procedure were
settled after the analyses had been run (registration, section 8). H3 is not
among them, because a prediction of no effect is not decided by a p-value.
The H4 row is the between-participant likelihood-ratio test only.
The full H4 criterion is the pair of bootstrap intervals in section 7.8.2, on
both dimensions, so a pass for that row here does not mean H4 passed.

```{r confirmatory-family}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The registered confirmatory family is four tests and no more: the attribution
# contrast on creativity, the attribution contrast on effort (those two
# together are H1, which is a conjunction and needs both), the
# attribution-by-dimension term from the joint model of section 7.6 (H2), and
# the likelihood-ratio test on the between-participant variance from section
# 7.8 (H4). H3 is not in the family: it is a prediction of no effect, decided
# by the equivalence procedure in section 7.10 (a test that the effect lies
# inside a stated bound) rather than by a corrected p-value.
#
# The Holm procedure. Order the four p-values from smallest to largest and
# compare the smallest against .05 divided by 4, the next against .05 divided
# by 3, the next against .05 divided by 2 and the largest against .05, stopping
# at the first comparison that fails. This holds the chance of any false
# positive across the whole family at 5 percent, and it is uniformly stricter
# than testing each p-value against .05 on its own. p.adjust() reports it as an
# adjusted p-value, the same decision rule expressed so that the threshold
# stays at .05 and the p-value moves instead.
#
# Which number goes in each slot.
#   - The two attribution contrasts are the estimated marginal contrasts from
#     the per-dimension models of sections 7.1 and 7.2, human minus generator,
#     averaged over image kind. They are not the raw TypeAI coefficients: under
#     treatment coding that coefficient is the attribution effect at
#     non-figurative images only, because the interaction term carries the
#     rest.
#   - The attribution-by-dimension slot is the Type x dimension row of the
#     joint model's type-III ANOVA. The contrast of contrasts printed in
#     section 7.6 is the same test written as a t rather than an F, and its
#     p-value agrees to within rounding.
#   - The H4 slot needs one p-value, but section 7.8 tests the two dimensions
#     separately. H4 predicts the structural shift on both, so like H1 it is a
#     conjunction, and a conjunction is only as strong as its weakest
#     component: we enter the larger of the two likelihood-ratio p-values.
#     Both are carried in the table beside it so nothing is hidden by the
#     choice. H4's support criterion is the pair of bootstrap intervals on the
#     two variance ratios in section 7.8.2, not this p-value, which enters the
#     family so that the family is complete, as the preregistration states.
#     The table's `note` column says this on the H4 row and states whether
#     the full criterion was met on each dimension, so the row cannot be read
#     as a pass for H4 as a whole.
#
# Convergence. Each slot's p-value is set to NA, with a note, if a fit behind
# it errored or did not converge (lmer_fit_status(), section 7; for H4 the
# two lme4 fits of the likelihood-ratio test on either dimension). The Holm
# step is told the family has four members whatever happens, so a missing
# p-value never makes the correction lighter for the others.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_confirmatory_family.csv"))

# Estimated marginal contrasts, human minus generator, averaged over image
# kind. adjust = "none" here is not a decision to leave the family
# uncorrected; it keeps emmeans from applying its own correction to a
# single contrast, so that the only correction applied anywhere is the Holm
# step below.
emm_contrast_p <- function(res, dim_name) {
  s <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(res$emm_main_Type, adjust = "none")))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1)
  usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
  tibble(hypothesis = "H1",
         test = paste0("Attribution contrast (Human - AI), ", dim_name,
                       ", estimated marginal, averaged over image kind"),
         estimate = s$estimate, se = s$SE, df = s$df,
         statistic = s$t.ratio, statistic_type = "t",
         p_raw = if (usable) s$p.value else NA_real_,
         fits_converged = usable,
         note = paste0("H1 is a conjunction: it needs both H1 rows to ",
                       "survive Holm.",
                       if (usable) "" else paste0(" ", fit_note(res$status))))
}

joint_int_row <- as.data.frame(joint_anova)["Type:dimension", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(joint_int_row) == 1)
joint_usable <- fit_usable(joint_status)

# The weaker of the two dimensions, chosen once by index so that every number
# reported in the H4 row belongs to the same fit. If either dimension's
# p-value is NA, the weaker one is unknown and the slot's p-value is NA.
h4_usable  <- !anyNA(h4_variance_test$lrt_between_p) &&
              all(h4_variance_test$between_fit_converged %in% TRUE)
h4_weakest <- which.max(replace(h4_variance_test$lrt_between_p,
                                is.na(h4_variance_test$lrt_between_p), -Inf))
h4_family  <- h4_variance_test[h4_weakest, ]

# The H4 note, built from the 7.8.2 verdicts so it always matches them.
h4_verdict_word <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "unavailable" else if (x) "yes" else "no"
h4_note <- paste0(
  "This row is the between-participant likelihood-ratio test only. The full ",
  "H4 criterion is the pair of bootstrap intervals in section 7.8.2 on each ",
  "dimension (between-participant ratio above 1 with its interval above 1, ",
  "residual ratio below 1 with its interval below 1), and passing Holm here ",
  "does not mean the H4 conjunction passed. Full criterion met: creativity ",
  h4_verdict_word(h4_variance_test$h4_supported[
    h4_variance_test$dimension == "creativity"]),
  ", effort ",
  h4_verdict_word(h4_variance_test$h4_supported[
    h4_variance_test$dimension == "effort"]),
  "; both dimensions ",
  h4_verdict_word(h4_variance_test$h4_supported_both_dimensions[1]), ".",
  if (h4_usable) "" else
    " A between-participant fit errored or did not converge, so the p-value is set to NA.")

confirmatory_family <- bind_rows(
  emm_contrast_p(creativity_res, "creativity"),
  emm_contrast_p(effort_res,     "effort"),
  tibble(hypothesis = "H2",
         test = "Attribution x dimension, joint model (type-III Satterthwaite)",
         estimate = joint_coc_tbl$estimate[1], se = joint_coc_tbl$SE[1],
         df = joint_int_row[["NumDF"]], statistic = joint_int_row[["F value"]],
         statistic_type = "F",
         p_raw = if (joint_usable) joint_int_row[["Pr(>F)"]] else NA_real_,
         fits_converged = joint_usable,
         note = paste0("H2 is claimed only if this row survives Holm and the ",
                       "ordinal version in study1_h2_ordinal.csv agrees with ",
                       "the raw-scale contrast in sign and significance.",
                       if (joint_usable) "" else
                         paste0(" ", fit_note(joint_status)))),
  tibble(hypothesis = "H4",
         test = paste0("Between-participant variance free by arm vs common, ",
                       "likelihood ratio (weaker of the two dimensions: ",
                       h4_family$dimension, ")"),
         estimate = h4_family$ratio_between_AI_over_Human,
         se = NA_real_,
         df = h4_family$lrt_between_df,
         statistic = h4_family$lrt_between_chisq,
         statistic_type = "chi-square",
         p_raw = if (h4_usable) h4_family$lrt_between_p else NA_real_,
         fits_converged = h4_usable,
         note = h4_note)
) %>%
  mutate(p_holm        = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = 4),
         survives_holm_at_05 = p_holm < .05,
         family_size   = n(),
         correction    = "Holm, family-wise alpha .05, four registered confirmatory tests",
         h4_creativity_lrt_p = h4_variance_test$lrt_between_p[
                                 h4_variance_test$dimension == "creativity"],
         h4_effort_lrt_p     = h4_variance_test$lrt_between_p[
                                 h4_variance_test$dimension == "effort"]) %>%
  relocate(hypothesis, test, estimate, se, df, statistic, statistic_type,
           p_raw, p_holm, survives_holm_at_05) %>%
  relocate(fits_converged, note, .after = everything())

# Four rows, and a p-value on every row whose fits converged.
stopifnot(nrow(confirmatory_family) == 4,
          all(!is.na(confirmatory_family$p_raw) |
                !confirmatory_family$fits_converged))

cat("=== Registered confirmatory family, Holm-corrected ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(confirmatory_family %>%
  select(hypothesis, test, estimate, statistic, statistic_type, p_raw, p_holm,
         survives_holm_at_05) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

cat("\nAll four survive at .05 after Holm: ",
    isTRUE(all(confirmatory_family$survives_holm_at_05)), "\n", sep = "")
cat("H1 is a conjunction and needs both of its rows: ",
    isTRUE(all(confirmatory_family$survives_holm_at_05[
      confirmatory_family$hypothesis == "H1"])), "\n", sep = "")
cat("H4 row: ", h4_note, "\n", sep = "")

write_csv(confirmatory_family,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_confirmatory_family.csv"))
```

---

# 7.10 H3: equivalence test on the attribution-by-image-kind interaction (registered)

H3 predicts that the attribution penalty is the same size for figurative and
non-figurative artworks. Nothing about a non-significant interaction
establishes that: a study that cannot detect a small difference will fail to
detect one whether or not it exists. The registered answer is an equivalence
test against a bound of plus or minus 0.20 rating points, run against the
model whose term it tests and repeated under the maximal random-effects
structure, because a simpler structure makes a prediction of no difference
easier to confirm, and the registration does not allow that. If the maximal
fit is singular, the registered fallback is the intercepts-only structure,
and the output records which structure the verdict rests on.

The bound was not set before the data were analysed. Section 8 of the
registration (`Docs/Preregistration/Study1_Preregistration.md`) records that
the bound and the decision table below were both settled after the analyses
had been run, so the H3 verdict rests on a bound chosen with the estimates
already in view.

```{r h3-equivalence}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# H3 predicts that the attribution penalty does not differ between figurative
# and non-figurative artworks. That is a prediction of no effect, and an
# ordinary significance test cannot deliver it: failing to detect a difference
# is not the same as showing there is none, because a small sample fails to
# detect everything. The registered answer is an equivalence test, meaning two
# one-sided tests: the estimate is tested once against the lower end of a
# stated bound and once against the upper end, each at .05, and equivalence is
# concluded only if both ends are rejected, which happens exactly when the
# 90 percent confidence interval lies entirely inside the bound.
#
# The quantity tested is the attribution-by-image-kind interaction, the
# `TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure` term of the per-dimension primary models fitted
# in sections 7.1 and 7.2. It is in rating points and says how much larger the
# attribution penalty is on figurative artworks than on non-figurative ones.
# The test sits here, beside the model whose term it tests, rather than in a
# separate robustness file, because the bound is on that model's own scale.
#
# The bound. Plus or minus 0.20 rating points, a fifth of a point on a
# five-point scale. It was settled after the analyses had been run, not
# before (registration, section 8). A difference between the
# two penalties smaller than that could not support a claim that the penalty
# depends on the kind of image, because it is finer than the resolution at
# which people use a five-point scale. Bounds of 0.30 and 0.50 rating points
# are reported alongside as descriptive sensitivity and carry no verdict.
#
# Why the random-effects structure matters more here than elsewhere, and why
# the effect runs one way. A random-effects structure that leaves out a slope
# the design warrants understates the standard error of the term. For an
# ordinary significance test that is anticonservative (too ready to call an
# effect significant) and runs against a researcher who predicts no effect,
# so a null result under the reduced structure is if anything harder to get.
# For an equivalence test the incentive reverses: a too-narrow interval fits
# inside the bound more easily, so the reduced structure makes the null
# prediction easier to confirm. H3 is therefore claimed only if equivalence
# holds under the maximal structure as well:
#
#     (1 + stimulus_type | id) + (1 + Type | stimulus_id)
#
# which is the structure fitted in section 7.5 and reused here rather than
# refitted, so the two sections cannot drift apart. Image kind varies within
# participant, so the by-participant slope is warranted; attribution varies
# between participants but within image, so the by-image slope is warranted.
# If that fit is singular, meaning the optimiser has pushed at least one
# variance or correlation to the edge of its range (the data cannot pin down
# that many parameters; it does not mean every slope is zero), the output
# says so and the H3 verdict is reported as resting on the reduced structure
# alone. Singularity is recorded, not tuned away.
#
# Convergence. Each row carries its fit's convergence and error status
# (lmer_fit_status(), section 7). A fit that errored or did not converge
# gives no test: its p-values, its equivalence flag and its verdict are NA,
# and its note says why. A maximal fit in that state is treated like an
# unavailable one, so the claim rests on the intercepts-only structure; an
# intercepts-only fit in that state leaves the claim NA.
#
# The decision table, which reads the significance test and the equivalence
# test together. Like the bound, it was settled after the analyses had been
# run (registration, section 8):
#   not significant + equivalent      -> supported
#   not significant + not equivalent  -> inconclusive (the design cannot
#                                        separate no effect from a small one)
#   significant     + equivalent      -> inconclusive (detectable but too small
#                                        to bear the claim)
#   significant     + not equivalent  -> rejected
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h3_equivalence.csv"))

H3_TERM             <- "TypeAI:stimulus_typeFigure"
H3_BOUND_REGISTERED <- 0.20
H3_BOUNDS_DESCRIPTIVE <- c(0.30, 0.50)
H3_ALPHA            <- 0.05   # per side, so the reported interval is 90 percent

# Two one-sided tests on one model term. The lower test asks whether the
# estimate is above -bound, the upper whether it is below +bound; the
# equivalence p-value is the larger of the two, because both have to pass.
# Satterthwaite degrees of freedom are taken from the fit, matching the
# per-dimension models; a fit without them is refused rather than tested with
# a normal approximation that would make every interval slightly too narrow.
tost_on_model_term <- function(fit, term, bound, alpha = H3_ALPHA) {
  co <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
  if (!term %in% rownames(co)) {
    stop("tost_on_model_term(): term '", term, "' is not in the fit. ",
         "Available: ", paste(rownames(co), collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (!"df" %in% colnames(co)) {
    stop("tost_on_model_term(): the fit carries no Satterthwaite degrees of ",
         "freedom. Refit with lmerTest::lmer().")
  }
  est <- co[term, "Estimate"]; se <- co[term, "Std. Error"]
  df  <- co[term, "df"];        nhst_p <- co[term, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  if (anyNA(c(est, se, df))) {
    stop("tost_on_model_term(): missing estimate, standard error or df for '",
         term, "'.")
  }
  p_lower <- pt((est + bound) / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  p_upper <- pt((est - bound) / se, df, lower.tail = TRUE)
  crit    <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  tost_p  <- max(p_lower, p_upper)
  tibble(term = term, bound_lo = -bound, bound_hi = bound,
         estimate = est, se = se, df = df,
         ci90_lo = est - crit * se, ci90_hi = est + crit * se,
         tost_p_lower = p_lower, tost_p_upper = p_upper, tost_p = tost_p,
         equivalent = tost_p < alpha,
         nhst_p = nhst_p, nhst_significant = nhst_p < .05)
}

# The registered four-cell verdict, from the two tests read together.
h3_verdict <- function(significant, equivalent) {
  if (is.na(significant) || is.na(equivalent)) return(NA_character_)
  if (!significant &&  equivalent) return("supported")
  if (!significant && !equivalent) return("inconclusive: cannot separate no effect from a small one")
  if ( significant &&  equivalent) return("inconclusive: detectable but too small to bear the claim")
  "rejected"
}

# The two structures. The intercepts-only fits are the primary models; the
# maximal fits are the section 7.5 objects, reused so that a single fit backs
# both sections.
H3_STRUCTURE_REDUCED <- "intercepts only: (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)"
H3_STRUCTURE_MAXIMAL <- "maximal: (1 + stimulus_type | id) + (1 + Type | stimulus_id)"

h3_fits <- list(
  list(dimension = "creativity", structure = H3_STRUCTURE_REDUCED,
       fit = creativity_res$fit, status = creativity_res$status),
  list(dimension = "effort",     structure = H3_STRUCTURE_REDUCED,
       fit = effort_res$fit,     status = effort_res$status),
  list(dimension = "creativity", structure = H3_STRUCTURE_MAXIMAL,
       fit = fullmax_creat$fit,  status = fullmax_creat$status),
  list(dimension = "effort",     structure = H3_STRUCTURE_MAXIMAL,
       fit = fullmax_eff$fit,    status = fullmax_eff$status)
)

# Singularity is read off each fit here rather than carried in by hand, so the
# column always describes the model that was actually tested.
h3_fits <- map(h3_fits, function(spec) {
  spec$singular <- if (inherits(spec$fit, "error")) NA
                   else lme4::isSingular(spec$fit, tol = 1e-4)
  spec
})

h3_equivalence <- map_dfr(h3_fits, function(spec) {
  bounds <- c(H3_BOUND_REGISTERED, H3_BOUNDS_DESCRIPTIVE)
  map_dfr(bounds, function(b) {
    role <- if (identical(b, H3_BOUND_REGISTERED)) "registered"
            else "descriptive sensitivity (no verdict)"
    out <- tryCatch({
      if (inherits(spec$fit, "error")) {
        stop("the fit for this structure failed: ",
             conditionMessage(spec$fit))
      }
      if (!fit_usable(spec$status)) {
        stop("the fit for this structure did not converge: ",
             spec$status$lme4_messages)
      }
      tost_on_model_term(spec$fit, H3_TERM, b)
    }, error = function(e) {
      message("H3 equivalence unavailable for ", spec$dimension, " / ",
              spec$structure, " at bound ", b, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
      tibble(term = H3_TERM, bound_lo = -b, bound_hi = b,
             estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
             ci90_lo = NA_real_, ci90_hi = NA_real_,
             tost_p_lower = NA_real_, tost_p_upper = NA_real_,
             tost_p = NA_real_, equivalent = NA,
             nhst_p = NA_real_, nhst_significant = NA)
    })
    out %>%
      mutate(dimension        = spec$dimension,
             random_structure = spec$structure,
             bound_role       = role,
             fit_singular     = spec$singular,
             verdict          = if (role == "registered")
                                  h3_verdict(nhst_significant, equivalent)
                                else NA_character_,
             alpha_per_side   = H3_ALPHA,
             fit_converged    = spec$status$converged,
             fit_error        = spec$status$fit_error,
             lme4_messages    = spec$status$lme4_messages,
             fit_note         = fit_note(spec$status,
                                         "test and the verdict")) %>%
      relocate(dimension, random_structure, bound_role, term, bound_lo,
               bound_hi, estimate, se, df, ci90_lo, ci90_hi)
  })
})

cat("=== H3: equivalence test on the attribution-by-image-kind interaction ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h3_equivalence %>%
  select(dimension, random_structure, bound_hi, bound_role, estimate, se,
         ci90_lo, ci90_hi, tost_p, equivalent, nhst_p, nhst_significant,
         fit_singular, verdict) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

# The registered claim needs the same verdict under both structures, on each
# dimension. A disagreement between them is reported as inconclusive rather
# than resolved in favour of either. That requirement presumes the maximal fit
# is one the data support. When it is singular (at least one random-effect
# variance or correlation at the boundary of its range, meaning the structure
# is richer than the data can pin down; on these data the boundary is reached
# by correlations at plus or minus one while the slope SDs stay above zero),
# the registered rule is the fallback to the intercepts-only structure: H3 is
# decided on that structure alone, `h3_structure_used` records that this is
# what happened, and the singular maximal result stays in the table for
# inspection without bearing on the claim. The same column names the
# structure in the ordinary case and when the maximal fit is unavailable
# altogether (it errored or did not converge), so `h3_claim` is always a
# verdict from the decision table, or NA when the intercepts-only fit itself
# gave no test.
h3_conclusion <- h3_equivalence %>%
  filter(bound_role == "registered") %>%
  group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(
    equivalent_intercepts_only =
      equivalent[grepl("^intercepts", random_structure)][1],
    equivalent_maximal =
      equivalent[grepl("^maximal", random_structure)][1],
    maximal_singular =
      fit_singular[grepl("^maximal", random_structure)][1],
    maximal_converged =
      fit_converged[grepl("^maximal", random_structure)][1],
    verdict_intercepts_only =
      verdict[grepl("^intercepts", random_structure)][1],
    verdict_maximal =
      verdict[grepl("^maximal", random_structure)][1],
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(structures_agree = !is.na(verdict_intercepts_only) &
                            !is.na(verdict_maximal) &
                            verdict_intercepts_only == verdict_maximal,
         h3_structure_used = case_when(
           is.na(verdict_intercepts_only) ~
             "none; the intercepts-only fit gave no test",
           !(maximal_converged %in% TRUE) ~
             "intercepts only; the maximal fit errored or did not converge",
           is.na(verdict_maximal) ~
             "intercepts only; the maximal fit is unavailable",
           maximal_singular %in% TRUE ~
             "intercepts only; the maximal fit is singular",
           TRUE ~ "both structures"),
         h3_claim = case_when(
           is.na(verdict_intercepts_only) ~ NA_character_,
           is.na(verdict_maximal)     ~ verdict_intercepts_only,
           maximal_singular %in% TRUE ~ verdict_intercepts_only,
           structures_agree           ~ verdict_intercepts_only,
           TRUE ~ "inconclusive: the two random-effects structures disagree"))

cat("\n=== H3: registered conclusion ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(h3_conclusion))

# The verdict in words, one dimension at a time, naming the structure it rests
# on. The singularity test is `%in% TRUE` rather than isTRUE() because the
# column holds one entry per dimension and each has to be checked on its own.
for (dn in h3_conclusion$dimension) {
  row <- h3_conclusion[h3_conclusion$dimension == dn, ]
  if (row$maximal_singular %in% TRUE) {
    cat(sprintf(paste0(
      "\nH3, %s: the maximal fit is singular, so the registered fallback ",
      "applies and the verdict rests on the intercepts-only structure alone: ",
      "%s. The equivalence result under the maximal structure (%s) is kept in ",
      "the table for inspection and carries no weight in the claim.\n"),
      dn, row$h3_claim, row$verdict_maximal))
  } else if (is.na(row$verdict_maximal)) {
    cat(sprintf(paste0(
      "\nH3, %s: the maximal fit is unavailable, so the verdict rests on the ",
      "intercepts-only structure alone: %s.\n"), dn, row$h3_claim))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(paste0(
      "\nH3, %s: decided under both structures (intercepts only: %s; ",
      "maximal: %s): %s.\n"),
      dn, row$verdict_intercepts_only, row$verdict_maximal, row$h3_claim))
  }
}

write_csv(h3_equivalence %>%
            left_join(h3_conclusion %>%
                        select(dimension, h3_claim, h3_structure_used),
                      by = "dimension"),
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_h3_equivalence.csv"))
```

# 7.11 Instrument sensitivity: the first figurative effort item

One of the twenty rating questions was worded differently from the others.
On the effort question for the first figurative image (1FigureEff), the two
highest options read "A lot of effort involved" and "Significant effort
involved"; on the other nine effort questions they read "Significant effort
involved" and "A great deal of effort involved". The item is scored as
answered, and the primary analysis keeps it. This section refits the two
registered quantities that use the effort ratings with that item removed and
sets them beside the full-sample values, so a reader can see whether the
item's wording moves either one. It is a sensitivity analysis and carries no
verdict.

```{r item-sensitivity}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What is refitted.
#   H1, effort. The registered H1 contrast (h1_contrast(), section 7): human
#     minus generator, averaged over the two image kinds with equal weight,
#     from the primary effort model fitted by the same function as section
#     7.2, on the effort ratings without the 111 ratings of 1FigureEff. The
#     figurative mean is then taken over four images and averaged with the
#     non-figurative mean over five. Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom, as in
#     the confirmatory family.
#   H2. The contrast of contrasts of section 7.6, (human minus generator on
#     effort) minus (human minus generator on creativity), averaged over image
#     kind, with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, on two reduced samples:
#       (a) without the 111 effort ratings of 1FigureEff, all creativity
#           ratings kept;
#       (b) without the image Figure_1 on both dimensions, so that the two
#           sides of the contrast rest on the same nine images.
#     The joint model keeps its registered random-effects rule: the
#     by-participant dimension slope, with the intercepts-only fallback if
#     that fit is singular or stops with an error.
#
# What each row carries. The estimate, its standard error, degrees of freedom
# and 95 percent confidence interval, its p-value, the difference from the
# full-sample estimate, the number of ratings used, the random-effects
# structure, and the fit's convergence, singularity and error status
# (lmer_fit_status(), section 7). A row whose fit errored or did not converge
# has its p-value set to NA and its note says why. The full-sample rows are
# read from the fits of sections 7.2 and 7.6 and are the registered numbers.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_item_sensitivity.csv"))

ITEM_SENS_STIMULUS  <- "Figure_1"   # stimulus_id of the image in 1FigureEff
ITEM_SENS_DIMENSION <- "effort"
ITEM_SENS_LABEL     <- "1FigureEff removed (effort rating of Figure_1)"
IMAGE_SENS_LABEL    <- "Figure_1 removed from both dimensions"

is_item <- function(d) {
  d$dimension == ITEM_SENS_DIMENSION & d$stimulus_id == ITEM_SENS_STIMULUS
}
stopifnot(sum(is_item(long)) == nrow(dat))   # one rating per participant

# --- H1, effort -------------------------------------------------------------
h1_eff_full <- h1_contrast(effort_res$fit) %>%
  mutate(sample = "full sample", n_ratings = nobs(effort_res$fit),
         random_structure = "(1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)",
         status = list(effort_res$status))

h1_eff_item_res <- fit_primary_lmm(
  "effort", data = long %>% filter(!is_item(long)) %>% droplevels())
h1_eff_item <- h1_contrast(h1_eff_item_res$fit) %>%
  mutate(sample = ITEM_SENS_LABEL, n_ratings = nobs(h1_eff_item_res$fit),
         random_structure = "(1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)",
         status = list(h1_eff_item_res$status))

# --- H2, joint contrast of contrasts ---------------------------------------
# The section 7.6 fitting rule, applied to a reduced sample.
fit_joint_rule <- function(d) {
  d <- d %>% droplevels() %>%
    mutate(stim_dim = interaction(stimulus_id, dimension, drop = TRUE))
  full <- tryCatch(
    lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type +
                     (1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stim_dim),
                   data = d, REML = TRUE, control = JOINT_CTRL),
    error = function(e) e)
  if (inherits(full, "error") || lme4::isSingular(full, tol = 1e-4)) {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::lmer(rating ~ Type * dimension * stimulus_type +
                       (1 | id) + (1 | stim_dim),
                     data = d, REML = TRUE, control = JOINT_CTRL),
      error = function(e) e)
    structure <- "(1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)  [fallback: full structure singular or unfittable]"
  } else {
    fit <- full
    structure <- "(1 + dimension | id) + (1 | stimulus_id:dimension)"
  }
  list(fit = fit, structure = structure, status = lmer_fit_status(fit))
}

joint_coc_of <- function(fit) {
  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ Type * dimension, lmer.df = "satterthwaite")
  coc <- emmeans::contrast(emm, interaction = c(Type = "pairwise",
                                                dimension = "revpairwise"))
  s  <- as.data.frame(summary(coc))
  ci <- as.data.frame(confint(coc))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1)
  tibble(estimate = s$estimate, se = s$SE, df = s$df,
         ci_low = ci$lower.CL, ci_high = ci$upper.CL, p = s$p.value)
}

h2_full <- joint_coc_tbl %>%
  transmute(estimate, se = SE, df, ci_low = lower.CL, ci_high = upper.CL,
            p = p.value) %>%
  mutate(sample = "full sample", n_ratings = nobs(joint_fit),
         random_structure = joint_structure, status = list(joint_status))

h2_reduced <- function(d, label) {
  jf <- fit_joint_rule(d)
  est <- if (inherits(jf$fit, "error"))
           tibble(estimate = NA_real_, se = NA_real_, df = NA_real_,
                  ci_low = NA_real_, ci_high = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
         else joint_coc_of(jf$fit)
  est %>% mutate(sample = label,
                 n_ratings = if (inherits(jf$fit, "error")) NA_integer_
                             else nobs(jf$fit),
                 random_structure = jf$structure,
                 status = list(jf$status))
}
h2_item  <- h2_reduced(joint_dat %>% filter(!is_item(joint_dat)),
                       ITEM_SENS_LABEL)
h2_image <- h2_reduced(joint_dat %>%
                         filter(stimulus_id != ITEM_SENS_STIMULUS),
                       IMAGE_SENS_LABEL)

# --- The table ---------------------------------------------------------------
item_sensitivity <- bind_rows(
  bind_rows(h1_eff_full, h1_eff_item) %>%
    mutate(hypothesis = "H1",
           quantity   = "Attribution contrast on effort (Human - AI), averaged over image kind"),
  bind_rows(h2_full, h2_item, h2_image) %>%
    mutate(hypothesis = "H2",
           quantity   = "(Human - AI | effort) - (Human - AI | creativity), averaged over image kind")
) %>%
  mutate(converged     = map_lgl(status, ~ .x$converged),
         singular      = map_lgl(status, ~ .x$singular),
         fit_error     = map_lgl(status, ~ .x$fit_error),
         lme4_messages = map_chr(status, ~ .x$lme4_messages),
         note          = map_chr(status, ~ fit_note(.x)),
         p             = if_else(converged & !fit_error, p, NA_real_)) %>%
  select(-status) %>%
  group_by(hypothesis) %>%
  mutate(difference_from_full = estimate - estimate[sample == "full sample"]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  relocate(hypothesis, quantity, sample, n_ratings, estimate, se, df,
           ci_low, ci_high, p, difference_from_full, random_structure,
           converged, singular, fit_error, lme4_messages, note)

stopifnot(nrow(item_sensitivity) == 5,
          sum(item_sensitivity$sample == "full sample") == 2)

cat("=== Instrument sensitivity: 1FigureEff ===\n")
print(as.data.frame(item_sensitivity %>%
  select(hypothesis, sample, n_ratings, estimate, se, ci_low, ci_high, p,
         difference_from_full, converged, singular) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))

# The reading in words: each reduced-sample estimate beside the full-sample
# one, and whether its interval still excludes zero. Description only.
for (i in which(item_sensitivity$sample != "full sample")) {
  r    <- item_sensitivity[i, ]
  full <- item_sensitivity %>%
    filter(hypothesis == r$hypothesis, sample == "full sample")
  cat(sprintf(paste0(
    "\n%s, %s: %.3f [%.3f, %.3f] against %.3f [%.3f, %.3f] on the full ",
    "sample, a difference of %+.3f rating points; the interval %s zero.\n"),
    r$hypothesis, r$sample, r$estimate, r$ci_low, r$ci_high,
    full$estimate, full$ci_low, full$ci_high, r$difference_from_full,
    if (is.na(r$ci_low)) "is unavailable and says nothing about"
    else if (r$ci_low > 0 || r$ci_high < 0) "excludes" else "includes"))
}

write_csv(item_sensitivity, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_item_sensitivity.csv"))
```
