# 8. Ordinal robustness check (CLMM)

```{r clmm}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cumulative-link mixed model with random intercepts for participant and
# stimulus. As a proportional-odds model, it gives each predictor the same
# effect at every cut point between adjacent ratings, and it treats the 1-5
# scale as ordered categories. If the LMM and CLMM agree on:
#   - the sign of the Type effect,
#   - the sign of the Type × StimulusType interaction, and
#   - whether each is significant at alpha = .05,
# then the continuity assumption of the LMM is defensible and we lead with
# the LMM in the paper. If they disagree, we lead with the CLMM.
#
# CLMMs with crossed random effects do not always converge. The fit uses the
# clmm defaults, the Laplace approximation (nAGQ = 1) and the nlminb
# optimizer.
#
# Convergence. A fit can stop with an error, or return without having
# converged. Both are recorded: `converged` is TRUE only when the optimizer's
# return code is 0 and the fit raised no warning about convergence, the
# Hessian or singularity, the same rule as the joint ordinal fit of section
# 7.6.1. The coefficients go to tables/study1_clmm_by_dimension.csv with that
# status on every row, and a fit that errored or did not converge has its
# p-values set to NA there, with a note.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, c("study1_clmm_creativity.rds",
                                           "study1_clmm_effort.rds")),
              file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_clmm_by_dimension.csv"))

fit_clmm <- function(dim_name) {

  dat_sub <- long %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(rating)) %>%
    mutate(
      # clmm requires an ordered factor as the response.
      rating_ord    = factor(rating, levels = 1:5, ordered = TRUE),
      Type          = relevel(factor(Type),          ref = "Human"),
      stimulus_type = relevel(factor(stimulus_type), ref = "NonFigure")
    )

  ordinal::clmm(
    rating_ord ~ Type * stimulus_type + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
    data = dat_sub,
    link = "logit",
    Hess = TRUE
  )
}

# Wrap in tryCatch so that a fit that stops with an error is reported and the
# notebook keeps running; warnings are captured so that a fit that returns
# without converging is reported too.
fit_clmm_with_status <- function(dim_name) {
  warns <- character(0)
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(
    tryCatch(fit_clmm(dim_name), error = function(e) e),
    warning = function(w) {
      warns <<- c(warns, conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    })
  failed <- inherits(fit, "error")
  list(fit = fit, warnings = warns, fit_error = failed,
       converged = !failed && isTRUE(fit$optRes$convergence == 0) &&
         !any(grepl("converge|Hessian|singular", warns, ignore.case = TRUE)),
       max_abs_gradient = if (failed) NA_real_ else max(abs(fit$gradient)),
       optimizer_message = if (failed) conditionMessage(fit)
                           else fit$optRes$message)
}

clmm_creativity_res <- fit_clmm_with_status("creativity")
clmm_effort_res     <- fit_clmm_with_status("effort")
clmm_creativity <- clmm_creativity_res$fit
clmm_effort     <- clmm_effort_res$fit

report_clmm <- function(res, dim_name, model_file) {
  if (res$fit_error) {
    cat("CLMM (", dim_name, ") stopped with an error: ",
        res$optimizer_message, "\n", sep = "")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat("\n=== CLMM ", stringr::str_to_title(dim_name), " ===\n", sep = "")
  cat("Converged:", res$converged, "| optimiser message:",
      res$optimizer_message, "| largest absolute gradient:",
      signif(res$max_abs_gradient, 3), "\n")
  if (length(res$warnings)) {
    cat("Warnings raised by the fit:", paste(res$warnings, collapse = " | "), "\n")
  }
  print(summary(res$fit))
  saveRDS(res$fit, file.path(PATH_OUT_MODELS, model_file))
}
report_clmm(clmm_creativity_res, "creativity", "study1_clmm_creativity.rds")
report_clmm(clmm_effort_res,     "effort",     "study1_clmm_effort.rds")

# One row per coefficient and dimension, on the log-odds latent scale, with
# the fit's status on every row.
clmm_table_for <- function(res, dim_name) {
  status_cols <- tibble(converged = res$converged, fit_error = res$fit_error,
                        singular = clmm_singular(res$fit),
                        max_abs_gradient = res$max_abs_gradient,
                        fit_messages = paste(c(res$optimizer_message,
                                               res$warnings), collapse = " | "),
                        note = if (res$fit_error)
                                 "fit stopped with an error, so no estimates"
                               else if (!res$converged)
                                 "fit did not converge, so the p-value is set to NA"
                               else "")
  if (res$fit_error) return(bind_cols(tibble(dimension = dim_name), status_cols))
  co <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(res$fit)))
  tibble(dimension = dim_name, term = rownames(co),
         estimate = co[, "Estimate"], se = co[, "Std. Error"],
         z = co[, "z value"],
         p = if (res$converged) co[, "Pr(>|z|)"] else NA_real_) %>%
    bind_cols(status_cols)
}
clmm_by_dimension <- bind_rows(clmm_table_for(clmm_creativity_res, "creativity"),
                               clmm_table_for(clmm_effort_res,     "effort"))
write_csv(clmm_by_dimension,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_clmm_by_dimension.csv"))
```

# 9. Aggregated Welch *t*-tests (continuity with prior report)

```{r welch-ttest}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For continuity with the aggregated-t-test analyses in the earlier report
# (Welch t-tests on per-participant averages collapsed across stimuli), that
# analysis is reproduced here so the LMM results can be placed beside it. The
# t-tests also serve as a check: their direction should match the LMM's, and
# only the size of the effect differs (the d from participant averages is
# larger, because averaging ten ratings removes the noise of a single
# rating; see section 9.1).
# The earlier report is the Welch t-test analysis of these data run in April
# 2025. Study 1 was shown at a lab meeting on 18 April 2025, and the authors'
# public DataBlitz talk (a short research presentation) on 26 September 2025
# showed these t-tests, so Study 1 results have already been presented in
# public. The dates and what each presentation showed are listed under
# question 1 of Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study1_AsPredicted.md.
# Section 8 of Docs/Preregistration/Study1_Preregistration.md marks which
# analysis decisions were made after estimates had been seen.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_welch_ttests.csv"))

agg_per_participant <- long %>%
  group_by(id, Type, dimension) %>%
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

run_welch <- function(dim_name) {
  agg_sub <- agg_per_participant %>% filter(dimension == dim_name)
  tt      <- t.test(mean_rating ~ Type, data = agg_sub)
  # Cohen's d with the pooled SD and without Hedges' correction (a
  # small-sample adjustment that shrinks d slightly), to match the earlier
  # report. This is the Welch-convention d. The registered d for the
  # manuscript is computed in §9.1 (same formula, bootstrap CI), and this one
  # must be labelled as the Welch/effectsize variant wherever it is printed.
  d_val   <- effectsize::cohens_d(mean_rating ~ Type, data = agg_sub)
  list(ttest = tt, d = d_val)
}

welch_creativity <- run_welch("creativity")
welch_effort     <- run_welch("effort")

cat("=== Welch t-test: creativity (AI vs Human, participant-averaged) ===\n")
print(welch_creativity$ttest); print(welch_creativity$d)

cat("\n=== Welch t-test: effort (AI vs Human, participant-averaged) ===\n")
print(welch_effort$ttest);     print(welch_effort$d)

# Write the summary for the paper.
welch_summary <- tribble(
  ~dimension,   ~t,                         ~df,                        ~p,                         ~d,
  "creativity", welch_creativity$ttest$statistic,
                welch_creativity$ttest$parameter,
                welch_creativity$ttest$p.value,
                welch_creativity$d$Cohens_d,
  "effort",     welch_effort$ttest$statistic,
                welch_effort$ttest$parameter,
                welch_effort$ttest$p.value,
                welch_effort$d$Cohens_d
)
write_csv(welch_summary, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_welch_ttests.csv"))
welch_summary
```

## 9.1 Registered effect-size convention (Cohen's *d* with bootstrap CI)

```{r bootstrap-d}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Cohen's d reported in the manuscript (registered).
#
# This file computes two other d's for the same contrast:
# emmeans::eff_size() on the LMM (standardized by the residual SD only,
# which ignores the participant and stimulus variance components and
# inflates d ~1.4x) and effectsize::cohens_d() inside run_welch() above. The
# 2026 registration fixes one convention (the paragraph on effect sizes in
# section 6 of Docs/Preregistration/Study1_Preregistration.md):
#
#   d = (M_Human - M_AI) / pooled SD,   computed on participant means
#       (one number per person per dimension, averaged over the 10 stimuli)
#   pooled SD = sqrt(((n_H - 1) s_H^2 + (n_A - 1) s_A^2) / (n_H + n_A - 2))
#   95% CI: nonparametric bootstrap, resampling participants within arm
#           (stratified), percentile interval, B = 10,000, seed 20260421.
#
# Positive d = Human-attributed work rated higher. Every other d in this
# pipeline (eff_size on the LMM in §7.1/7.2, the Welch d in §9) must be
# labeled by its convention wherever it is printed and must not be called
# "Cohen's d" without qualification in the manuscript.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

BOOT_B    <- 10000L
BOOT_SEED <- 20260421L
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_bootstrap_d.csv"))

pooled_d <- function(x_h, x_a) {
  n_h <- length(x_h); n_a <- length(x_a)
  sp  <- sqrt(((n_h - 1) * var(x_h) + (n_a - 1) * var(x_a)) / (n_h + n_a - 2))
  (mean(x_h) - mean(x_a)) / sp
}

bootstrap_d_for <- function(dim_name) {
  agg_sub <- agg_per_participant %>%
    filter(dimension == dim_name, !is.na(mean_rating))
  x_h <- agg_sub$mean_rating[agg_sub$Type == "Human"]
  x_a <- agg_sub$mean_rating[agg_sub$Type == "AI"]
  stopifnot(length(x_h) > 2, length(x_a) > 2)
  d_obs <- pooled_d(x_h, x_a)
  set.seed(BOOT_SEED)   # reset per dimension so each is independently reproducible
  d_boot <- vapply(seq_len(BOOT_B), function(b) {
    pooled_d(sample(x_h, length(x_h), replace = TRUE),
             sample(x_a, length(x_a), replace = TRUE))
  }, numeric(1))
  ci <- unname(quantile(d_boot, c(0.025, 0.975), type = 7))
  tibble(
    dimension  = dim_name,
    d          = d_obs,
    ci_lo      = ci[1],
    ci_hi      = ci[2],
    n_human    = length(x_h),
    n_ai       = length(x_a),
    B          = BOOT_B,
    seed       = BOOT_SEED,
    convention = "(M_Human - M_AI) / pooled SD on participant means; stratified percentile bootstrap"
  )
}

bootstrap_d <- bind_rows(bootstrap_d_for("creativity"),
                         bootstrap_d_for("effort"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(bootstrap_d$d), !anyNA(bootstrap_d$ci_lo),
          all(bootstrap_d$ci_lo <= bootstrap_d$d),
          all(bootstrap_d$d <= bootstrap_d$ci_hi))

# The second registered effect size, reported beside the first rather than
# instead of it. The d above averages each person's ten ratings before
# comparing the arms, which strips out the noise of a single rating and makes
# the number larger than the conventional small-medium-large benchmarks were
# built for. The registration therefore also asks for a model-based
# standardised effect: the attribution effect divided by the square root of
# the summed variance components. The variance components are the three
# quantities the primary mixed model estimates: how much participants differ
# from one another, how much images differ from one another, and the remainder
# left over once both are taken out. Their sum is the model's estimate of the
# total spread of a single rating, so dividing by its square root puts the
# effect in units of one rating rather than of a ten-rating average, which is
# the scale the between-subject effect sizes in the surrounding literature use.
#
# The numerator is the estimated marginal contrast, human minus generator,
# averaged over image kind, the same quantity section 7.9 puts in the
# confirmatory family. The raw TypeAI coefficient would be the wrong
# numerator, because under treatment coding it is the attribution effect at
# non-figurative images only.
model_based_d_for <- function(res, dim_name) {
  contrast_row <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(res$emm_main_Type,
                                              adjust = "none")))
  stopifnot(nrow(contrast_row) == 1)
  total_var <- sum(as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(res$fit))$vcov)
  tibble(dimension = dim_name,
         d_model_based = contrast_row$estimate / sqrt(total_var),
         model_based_total_sd = sqrt(total_var))
}

bootstrap_d <- bootstrap_d %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(model_based_d_for(creativity_res, "creativity"),
                      model_based_d_for(effort_res,     "effort")),
            by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(model_based_convention = paste0(
    "estimated marginal contrast (Human - AI, averaged over image kind) / ",
    "sqrt(participant + image + remainder variance) from the primary model"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(bootstrap_d$d_model_based))

bootstrap_d
write_csv(bootstrap_d, file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_bootstrap_d.csv"))
# The two columns answer different questions and are not interchangeable:
# `d` is on the scale of a person's average rating and `d_model_based` on the
# scale of one rating, so `d` is the larger of the two by construction. Each is
# labelled by its convention in the deposited file, and the manuscript names
# which one it is quoting wherever either appears.
# The point estimate must equal the Welch d in study1_welch_ttests.csv up to
# sign convention (effectsize::cohens_d uses the same pooled-SD formula on the
# same participant means); only the CI method differs.
```

# 10. Stimulus-level sensitivity

```{r stim-sensitivity}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For each of the 10 stimuli, compute the AI-vs-Human contrast on creativity
# and effort separately, using unpaired Welch t-tests on that stimulus's
# ratings alone. The aim is to see whether any single image is an outlier,
# for example whether two of the ten images drive the pooled effect.
# A forest plot (section 11.2) draws these 10 estimates with their intervals
# and a dashed reference line at zero, no difference between the arms.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_per_stimulus_contrasts.csv"))

per_stim_contrasts <- long %>%
  group_by(dimension, stimulus_id) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    x_h <- .x$rating[.x$Type == "Human"]
    x_a <- .x$rating[.x$Type == "AI"]
    x_h <- x_h[!is.na(x_h)]
    x_a <- x_a[!is.na(x_a)]
    if (length(x_h) < 3 | length(x_a) < 3) {
      return(tibble(diff = NA, ci_lo = NA, ci_hi = NA, p = NA,
                    n_ai = length(x_a), n_hum = length(x_h)))
    }
    # t.test(x_h, x_a) tests the ordering Human - AI directly. Both the
    # point estimate and the CI from this call are on the Human - AI scale,
    # so positive values mean "rated higher when attributed to Human." The
    # difference of means is computed directly (rather than backed out via
    # diff(estimate)) so its sign cannot come out reversed.
    tt <- t.test(x_h, x_a, var.equal = FALSE)
    tibble(
      diff  = mean(x_h) - mean(x_a),
      ci_lo = tt$conf.int[1],
      ci_hi = tt$conf.int[2],
      p     = tt$p.value,
      n_ai  = length(x_a),
      n_hum = length(x_h)
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

per_stim_contrasts

write_csv(per_stim_contrasts,
          file.path(PATH_OUT_TAB, "study1_per_stimulus_contrasts.csv"))
```

# 11. Figures

## 11.1 Main figure: condition × dimension violins

```{r fig-main, fig.width=7, fig.height=9}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main figure for the paper: a violin (the shape of the distribution), a
# boxplot and the jittered participant means, one panel per dimension,
# stacked vertically. The x-axis is Creator Type. A vertical layout suits a
# single-column Nature Communications figure.
#
# The data shown are participant-level means (one dot per participant per
# cell), so the figure shows the unit of analysis of the aggregated t-test
# and roughly matches the LMM's fixed-effect estimates.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
clear_outputs(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG, c("study1_fig1_main.pdf",
                                        "study1_fig1_main.png")),
              file.path(PATH_PAPER_FIG, "study1_fig1_main.pdf"))

participant_cell <- long %>%
  group_by(id, Type, dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_mean = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    dimension = factor(stringr::str_to_title(as.character(dimension)),
                       levels = c("Creativity", "Effort"))
  )

# The jitter is horizontal only (height = 0). A vertical jitter would nudge
# participant means that sit exactly at 1 or 5 past the ends of the scale,
# and a y-axis limit set through scale_y_continuous() would then drop those
# points from the plot. coord_cartesian() zooms the axis to 1..5 without
# dropping anything, so every participant is drawn. The seed makes the
# jitter offsets identical on every knit.
set.seed(20260421)
fig_main <- ggplot(participant_cell,
                   aes(x = Type, y = rating_mean, fill = Type)) +
  geom_violin(width = 0.9, alpha = 0.55,
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
              trim = FALSE) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.25, alpha = 0.75, outlier.shape = NA,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = Type), width = 0.08, height = 0,
              alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ dimension, ncol = 1, strip.position = "left") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, 5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = PALETTE_TYPE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = PALETTE_TYPE) +
  labs(x = "Creator Type", y = "Participant mean rating (1–5)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position   = "none",
    strip.background  = element_blank(),
    strip.placement   = "outside",
    strip.text        = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y      = element_blank(),
    axis.text         = element_text(color = "black"),
    plot.margin       = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

fig_main

# Save both to analysis folder (for this notebook's record) and to the
# Final Paper folder (for Overleaf to pick up directly). PDF for LaTeX,
# PNG for quick inspection.
ggsave(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG,   "study1_fig1_main.pdf"),
       fig_main, width = 5.5, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
ggsave(file.path(PATH_OUT_FIG,   "study1_fig1_main.png"),
       fig_main, width = 5.5, height = 8, dpi = 300)
ggsave(file.path(PATH_PAPER_FIG, "study1_fig1_main.pdf"),
       fig_main, width = 5.5, height = 8, device = cairo_pdf)
```

**Run order for these outputs to exist:** every chunk from `run-record`
onward (`clear_outputs()` and the run identifier come from `run-record`;
`dat`, `long` and every model derive from `working`, which the §2.2 join
builds). Every chunk from `lmm-helpers` onward uses its helpers
(`lmer_fit_status()`, `h1_contrast()`), and every chunk from
`tidy-stat-tables` onward uses `with_status()`. Chunks
`lmm-fully-maximal`, `lmm-joint`, `lmm-diagnostics` and `bootstrap-d`
require `lmm-creativity` / `lmm-effort` to have run first. The
`lmm-diagnostics` chunk performs 242 `lmer` refits (2 dimensions × (111 +
10)) and takes a few minutes.

The three H4 chunks (`h4-variance-partition`, `h4-variance-test`,
`h4-descriptive`) need `pivot-long` and `lmm-helpers`; `h4-variance-test`
also runs the participant bootstrap (1,000 resamples per dimension, two
refits each) and takes about a minute and a half. `lmm-joint-ordinal` needs
`lmm-joint`, because its raw-scale row is read from that chunk's fitted
object. `confirmatory-family` needs `lmm-creativity`, `lmm-effort`,
`lmm-joint` and `h4-variance-test`, because it collects one *p*-value from
each. `h3-equivalence` needs `lmm-creativity`, `lmm-effort` and
`lmm-fully-maximal`, since it reuses the section 7.5 fits for the maximal
structure rather than fitting them a second time. `item-sensitivity` needs
`lmm-effort` and `lmm-joint`. `clmm` needs `lmm-joint-ordinal` for
`clmm_singular()`. `run-manifest` runs last.

**`Docs/Writing/Final Paper/figures/`** (paper-ready figure copies):

- `study1_fig1_main.pdf`
- `study1_fig2_forest.pdf`

The integration notebook (`Study1_03_Integration.Rmd`) consumes the
`models/*.rds` and `tables/*.csv` outputs from the analysis folder and
writes LaTeX stat fragments directly into `Docs/Writing/Final Paper/tables/`
where Overleaf can `\\input{}` them.

## 13.1 Run manifest

The last chunk lists every output this run was responsible for, says for
each whether this run wrote it, and records its checksum. Because the
previous manifest is deleted when the run starts, a manifest on disk means
the run reached its last chunk.

```{r run-manifest}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One row per path registered through clear_outputs(), in the order the
# chunks registered them, the input record of section 1.2 among them:
#   run_id            this run's identifier (section 1.2).
#   file              the path, relative to this Study 1 folder, or under
#                     Docs/Writing/Final Paper/ for the paper copies.
#   written_this_run  TRUE when the file exists and its modification time is
#                     no earlier than the second in which this run started.
#                     Every listed file was deleted at the top of the chunk
#                     that writes it, so FALSE means that chunk wrote nothing
#                     (a model whose fit failed is not saved, for example).
#   sha256            the file's SHA-256 checksum, NA when it does not exist.
# The manifest does not list itself.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
manifest_label <- function(p) {
  if (startsWith(p, paste0(PATH_OUT, "/"))) {
    return(substring(p, nchar(PATH_OUT) + 2))
  }
  if (startsWith(p, paste0(PATH_PAPER, "/"))) {
    return(file.path("Docs", "Writing", "Final Paper",
                     substring(p, nchar(PATH_PAPER) + 2)))
  }
  p
}

manifest_paths <- setdiff(QUANT_OUTPUTS, PATH_RUN_MANIFEST)
run_start_sec  <- trunc(RUN_START, units = "secs")
exists_now     <- file.exists(manifest_paths)
run_manifest <- tibble(
  run_id           = RUN_ID,
  file             = vapply(manifest_paths, manifest_label, character(1),
                            USE.NAMES = FALSE),
  written_this_run = exists_now &
                     file.mtime(manifest_paths) >= run_start_sec,
  sha256           = ifelse(exists_now,
                            unname(tools::sha256sum(manifest_paths)),
                            NA_character_)
) %>%
  mutate(written_this_run = coalesce(written_this_run, FALSE))

cat("Outputs listed:", nrow(run_manifest),
    "| written this run:", sum(run_manifest$written_this_run),
    "| not written:", sum(!run_manifest$written_this_run), "\n")
if (any(!run_manifest$written_this_run)) {
  cat("Not written this run:\n")
  print(run_manifest$file[!run_manifest$written_this_run])
}
write_csv(run_manifest, PATH_RUN_MANIFEST)
```
